title: -ly
text: The suffix -ly in English is usually a contraction of "-like", similar to the Anglo-Saxon "lice" and German "lich".

title: -ly
text: It is commonly added to an adjective to form an adverb, but in some cases it is used to form an adjective, such as "ugly" or "manly".

title: -ly
text: The adjective to which the suffix is added may have been lost from the language, as in the case of "early", in which the Anglo-Saxon word "aer" only survives in the poetic usage "ere".

title: 1974 aluminum cent
text: The 1974 aluminum cent was a one-cent coin proposed by the United States Mint in 1973.

title: 1974 aluminum cent
text: It was composed of an alloy of aluminum and trace metals, and intended to replace the predominantly copper–zinc cent due to the rising costs of coin production in the traditional bronze alloy.

title: 1974 aluminum cent
text: 1,571,167 were struck in anticipation of release, but none were released into circulation.

title: 1974 aluminum cent
text: Examples were passed out to US Congressmen in a bid to win favor in switching to the new alloy.

title: 1974 aluminum cent
text: When the proposed aluminum cent was rejected, the Mint recalled and destroyed the examples.

title: 1974 aluminum cent
text: A few aluminum cents not returned to the Mint are believed to remain in existence.

title: 1974 aluminum cent
text: One example was donated to the Smithsonian Institution, while another was alleged to have been found by a US Capitol Police Officer.

title: 1974 aluminum cent
text: A 1974-D specimen was found in January 2014 by Randall Lawrence, who said it was a retirement gift to his father, who worked at the Mint in Denver.

title: 1974 aluminum cent
text: Randall planned on selling it in a public auction, but the Mint demanded its return, saying that the coin was never authorized for release and therefore remains U.S. Government property.

title: 1974 aluminum cent
text: Lawrence (and his business partner at their coin store, Michael McConnell) ultimately surrendered the coin when the Mint showed that the aluminum penny had never been authorized to be struck in Denver, and there was no evidence that the coin had been a gift of any kind.

title: 52nd Infantry Division (German Empire)

text: The division was initially mixed, with two infantry regiments from the Grand Duchy of Baden, one infantry regiment from Prussian Saxony, and Prussian and Baden support units (cavalry, artillery, engineers, and service and support units).

text: While the infantry regiments and the divisional cavalry squadron were regular army units, the rest of the division was made up of reserve units and units formed during the war.

title: 52nd Infantry Division (German Empire)

title: 52nd Infantry Division (German Empire)
text: The 52nd Infantry Division became more Baden as the war progressed, as the 66th Magdeburg Infantry Regiment, the regiment from Prussian Saxony, was replaced on April 6, 1917, by Baden's 111th Infantry Regiment "Margrave Ludwig Wilhelm".

title: Adelaide leak
text: The Adelaide leak was the revelation to the press of a dressing-room incident during the third Test, a cricket match played during the 1932–33 Ashes series between Australia and England, more commonly known as the Bodyline series.

title: Adelaide leak
text: During the course of play on 14 January 1933, the Australian Test captain Bill Woodfull was struck over the heart by a ball delivered by Harold Larwood.

title: Adelaide leak
text: Although not badly hurt, Woodfull was shaken and dismissed shortly afterwards.

title: Adelaide leak
text: On his return to the Australian dressing room, Woodfull was visited by the managers of the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC) team, Pelham Warner and Richard Palairet.

title: Adelaide leak
text: Warner enquired after Woodfull's health, but the latter dismissed his concerns in brusque fashion.

title: Adelaide leak
text: He said he did not want to speak to the Englishman owing to the Bodyline tactics England were using, leaving Warner embarrassed and shaken.

title: Adelaide leak
text: The matter became public knowledge when someone present leaked the exchange to the press and it was widely reported on 16 January.

title: Adelaide leak
text: Such leaks to the press were practically unknown at the time, and the players were horrified that the confrontation became public knowledge.

title: Bibliography of Abraham Lincoln
text: This bibliography of Abraham Lincoln is a comprehensive list of written and published works about or by Abraham Lincoln, 16th President of the United States.

title: Bifurcation theory
text: Bifurcation theory is the mathematical study of changes in the qualitative or topological structure of a given family, such as the integral curves of a family of vector fields, and the solutions of a family of differential equations. Most commonly applied to the mathematical study of dynamical systems, a bifurcation occurs when a small smooth change made to the parameter values (the bifurcation parameters) of a system causes a sudden 'qualitative' or topological change in its behaviour.

title: Bifurcation theory
text: Bifurcations occur in both continuous systems (described by ODEs, DDEs or PDEs) and discrete systems (described by maps).

title: Bifurcation theory
text: The name "bifurcation" was first introduced by Henri Poincaré in 1885 in the first paper in mathematics showing such a behavior.

title: Bifurcation theory
text: Henri Poincaré also later named various types of stationary points and classified them.

title: Bill Ponsford
text: William Harold "Bill" Ponsford (19 October 1900 – 6 April 1991) was an Australian cricketer.

title: Bill Ponsford

title: Bill Ponsford

title: Bill Woodfull
text: William Maldon "Bill" Woodfull OBE (22 August 1897 – 11 August 1965) was an Australian cricketer of the 1920s and 1930s.

title: Bill Woodfull

title: Bill Woodfull

title: Bill Woodfull

title: Bill Woodfull
text: His opening pairing with fellow Victorian Bill Ponsford for both his state and Australia remains one of the most successful in history.

title: Bill Woodfull

text: She competed in the women's duet competition with her twin sister, Isabela Moraes, at both the 2000 and 2004 Summer Olympics .

title: Carolina Moraes
text: Both also competed for Ohio State University, winning 11 national championships, including the team routine title in 2000, and four straight titles in duet and trio routines between 1999 and 2002.

title: Carolina Moraes
text: Following the Olympics, Carolina and Isabela retired and joined Cirque du Soleil, with their first performance being as part of the 2005 World Aquatics Championships opening ceremony.

title: Carolina Moraes
text: Both have been part of the cast of "Le Rêve", a show presented in Las Vegas since 2007, though Carolina is less frequent as she travels with her husband, part of Cirque du Soleil's technical team.

title: Carrie (2013 film)
text: Carrie is a 2013 American supernatural horror film, directed by Kimberly Peirce, and is the third film adaptation of Stephen King's 1974 novel of the same name.

title: Carrie (2013 film)
text: The film was produced by Kevin Misher, with a screenplay by Lawrence D. Cohen & Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa.

title: Carrie (2013 film)
text: The film was released by Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer and Screen Gems on October 18, 2013.

title: Carrie (2013 film)
text: The film stars Chloë Grace Moretz as the titular Carrie White, Julianne Moore as Carrie's mother Margaret White, Judy Greer as Ms. Desjardin, Portia Doubleday as Chris Hargensen, Gabriella Wilde as Sue Snell, Ansel Elgort as Tommy Ross, and Alex Russell as Billy Nolan.

title: Carrie Marcus Neiman
text: Carrie Marcus Neiman (May 3, 1883 – March 6, 1953) was an American businessperson and one of the cofounders of Neiman Marcus, a luxury department store.

title: Casey (song)
text: "Casey" is a song written by Darren Hayes and Peter-John Vettese for Hayes' album "This Delicate Thing We've Made".

title: Casey (song)
text: It was released as the fourth and final single from the album, and was his first single to be a download-only release.

title: Casey (song)
text: It managed to chart at #108 in the UK.

title: Casey (song)
text: The original version of the song does not appear on any of the download singles, however a radio edit was made and released.

title: Casey (song)
text: An eighty-second clip of the music video was released by Hayes on his YouTube account on 22 December 2007.

title: Casey (song)
text: The full clip debuted on Hayes' official website and YouTube account on 26 January 2008.

title: Cast coinage
text: Cast coinage refers to coins made by pouring melted metal into a mold, i.e. casting.

title: Cast coinage
text: It has been used for regular coins, particularly in the Far East, but also on a smaller scale.

title: Cast coinage
text: (e.g.: the ancient Mediterranean world.)

title: Cast coinage
text: The method differs from the current mode of coin production, which is done by striking coin blanks that have been cut out of metal sheets.

title: Cast coinage
text: The method has also been used by forgers.

title: Casuarinaceae
text: The Casuarinaceae are a family of dicotyledonous flowering plants placed in the order Fagales, consisting of four genera and 91 species of trees and shrubs native to the Australia, Southeast Asia, Malesia, Papuasia, and the Pacific Islands.

title: Casuarinaceae
text: At one time, all species were placed in the genus "Casuarina".

title: Casuarinaceae
text: Lawrie A. S. Johnson separated out many of those species and renamed them into the new genera of "Gymnostoma" in 1980 and 1982, "Allocasuarina" in 1982, and "Ceuthostoma" in 1988, with some additional formal descriptions of new species in each other genus.

title: Casuarinaceae
text: At the time, it was somewhat controversial.

title: Casuarinaceae
text: The monophyly of these genera was later supported in a 2003 genetics study of the family.

title: Casuarinaceae
text: In the Wettstein system, this family was the only one placed in the order Verticillatae.

title: Casuarinaceae
text: Likewise, in the Engler, Cronquist, and Kubitzki systems, the Casuarinaceae were the only family placed in the order Casuarinales.

title: Cathedral of Petrópolis
text: The Cathedral of Saint Peter of Alcantara (Portuguese: "Catedral de São Pedro de Alcântara" ), also known as the Cathedral of Petrópolis, is a Roman Catholic cathedral in Petrópolis, Brazil.

title: Cathedral of Petrópolis
text: The cathedral is dedicated to Saint Peter of Alcantara, the patron saint of Brazil.

title: Cathedral of Petrópolis
text: Is also home of the Imperial Mausoleum of the Brazilian Imperial Family.

title: Cay (volcano)
text: Cay is a stratovolcano in the South Volcanic Zone of the Andes in Aysén del General Carlos Ibáñez del Campo Region, Chile.

title: Cay (volcano)
text: The volcano is located 15 km northeast of the larger Maca Volcano and about 230 km of the Chile Trench at the intersection of NW-SE and NE-SW faults of the Liquiñe-Ofqui Fault Zone.

title: Cay (volcano)
text: The volcano is composed from basalt and dacite and there is no evidence of Holocene activity.

title: Cay (volcano)
text: Below 1000m, several parasitic cones lie on the southwest flank of the volcano.

title: Celebrity Home Entertainment
text: Celebrity Home Entertainment (also known as simply "Celebrity Video"), founded by Noel C. Bloom in 1985, was a home video distributor specializing in mostly obscure material from around the world, as well as B-grade action films and soft-core adult fare, although they also released some material that was very famous at the time of its original release (such as "BraveStarr", "Filmation's Ghostbusters", "C.O.P.S." and the ).

title: Celina Seghi
text: Celina Seghi (born 6 March 1920) is a former Italian alpine skier.

title: Celina Seghi
text: Born in Abetone, Tuscany, she was the youngest child in a family of nine and earned her first Italian championship medal, a bronze in the slalom, in 1934.

title: Celina Seghi
text: In 1937 she earned three national titles, her first victories at that level, by winning the slalom, downhill, and combined events.

title: Celina Seghi
text: In total she won a total of 25 gold, 6 silver, and 3 bronze medals at the Italian National Championships: gold seven times, silver thrice, and bronze twice in the downhill, gold and silver once each in the giant slalom, gold ten times, silver twice, and bronze once in the slalom, and gold seven times in the combined.

title: Cenk Celebioglu
text: Cenk Celebioglu is a Turkish-born composer whose orchestral compositions combine electronic and live instruments.

title: Cenk Celebioglu
text: He aspires to use his music to establish a bridge between east and west.

title: Cenk Celebioglu
text: He attended Berklee College of Music.

title: Cenk Celebioglu
text: Famous composer Fahir Atakoglu, whom he admired since his young age, has offered much encouragement to Cenk, as he is now dedicated to continue his professional career in creating his own unique music and orchestration for film, trailer & media

title: Center Street Historic District (Ashland, Ohio)
text: Center Street Historic District is a historic district in Ashland, Ohio, United States.

title: Center Street Historic District (Ashland, Ohio)
text: Placed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1976 with a boundary increase that took place in 1992, Center Street features Victorian homes built in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

title: Center Street Historic District (Ashland, Ohio)
text: The district is established between Town Creek and Vernon Avenue on the east side of Center Street and between the theater and Morgan Avenue on the west side.

title: Center Street Historic District (Ashland, Ohio)
text: Once known as Huron Road, Center Street runs current with Ohio State Route 511 and Ohio State Route 60, which travels the entire length of Ohio.

title: Center Street Historic District (Ashland, Ohio)
text: The Center Street Historic District Association is the homeowners' association for the district.

title: Central Avenue Historic District (Dayton, Ohio)
text: The Central Avenue Historic District is a small segment of the larger Grafton Hill neighborhood of Dayton, Ohio, United States.

title: Central Avenue Historic District (Dayton, Ohio)
text: Composed of just two blocks near the border between Grafton Hill and Dayton View, the historic district comprises a cohesive collection of houses dating primarily from the turn of the 20th century, and it has been named a historic site.

title: Chaconne in D minor (Pachelbel)
text: Chaconne in D minor (PWC 41, T. 204, PC 147, POP 14) is an organ chaconne by Johann Pachelbel.

title: Chaconne in D minor (Pachelbel)
text: It is one of the six surviving chaconnes by the composer, and one of his best known organ works.

title: Chaconne in F minor (Pachelbel)
text: Chaconne in F minor (PWC 43, T. 206, PC 149, POP 16) is an organ chaconne by Johann Pachelbel.

title: Chaconne in F minor (Pachelbel)
text: One of the six surviving chaconnes by the composer, it is one of his best known organ works.

title: Change Has Come
text: Change Has Come was the only recording the Screaming Trees released through Sub Pop.

title: Change Has Come
text: Released in 1990 the Screaming Trees then moved on to a major label, Epic Records, for their next three albums - "Uncle Anesthesia", "Sweet Oblivion," and "Dust", as well as the "Something About Today" EP.

title: Chanhassen High School
text: Chanhassen High School (CNS) is a public high school located in Chanhassen, Minnesota, a southwestern suburb of the Minneapolis-Saint Paul area.

title: Chanhassen High School
text: CNS has a grade 9–12 school program.

title: Chanhassen High School
text: Construction of the school was approved by voters in 2006 in response to rapidly growing enrollment in Carver County and overcrowding at Chaska High School, the district's other high school.

title: Chanhassen High School
text: Chanhassen had an enrollment of 1,576 students during the 2014-15 school year, with an 18:1 student teacher ratio.

title: Chanhassen High School
text: There are 82 teachers at the school, and more than 80 percent of them have a master's degree or higher.

title: Chanhassen High School
text: The student body makeup is 52 percent male and 48 percent female, and the total minority enrollment is 9 percent.

title: Chaos Marauders
text: Chaos Marauders is a card-based board game for 2-4 players designed by Stephen Hand, illustrated by John Blanche and was published by Games Workshop in 1987.

title: Chaos Marauders
text: A second edition was published by Fantasy Flight Games in 2009.

title: Chapel Hill Transit
text: Chapel Hill Transit operates public bus and van transportation services within the contiguous municipalities of Chapel Hill and Carrboro and the campus of the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in the southeast corner of Orange County in the Research Triangle metropolitan region of North Carolina.

title: Chapel Hill Transit
text: Chapel Hill Transit began operation in August 1974.

title: Chapel Hill Transit
text: Total ridership, including fixed route, EZ Rider and Shared Ride Feeder service, for fiscal year 2015 was almost 6.5 million ridership.

title: Charles Alvin Beckwith
text: Charles Alvin "Charlie" Beckwith (January 22, 1929 – June 13, 1994), known as Chargin' Charlie, was a career U.S. Army Special Forces officer best remembered as helping create Delta Force, the premier counter terrorism and asymmetrical warfare unit of the U.S. Army.

title: Charles Alvin Beckwith
text: He served in the Malayan Emergency and the Vietnam War, and attained the rank of colonel before his retirement.

title: Charles Evers
text: James Charles Evers (born September 11, 1922) is an American civil rights activist and former politician.

title: Charles Evers
text: A Republican, Evers was known for his role in the Civil Rights Movement along with his younger brother Medgar Evers.

title: Charles Evers
text: He was made the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) State Voter Registration Chairman in 1954.

title: Charles Evers
text: After his brother's assassination in 1963, Evers took over his position as field director of the NAACP in Mississippi.

title: Charles Evers
text: As field director, Evers organized and led many demonstrations for the rights of African Americans.

title: Charleston, Missouri
text: Charleston is a city in Mississippi County, Missouri, United States.

title: Charleston, Missouri
text: The population was 5,947 at the 2010 census.

title: Charleston, Missouri
text: It is the county seat of Mississippi County.

title: Charleston, Missouri
text: It is a home to a local correctional facility.

title: Chawalit Kamutchati
text: Chawalit Kamutchati (born 6 March 1937) is a Thai former sports shooter.

title: Chawalit Kamutchati
text: He competed in the 50 metre rifle, three positions event at the 1972 Summer Olympics.

title: Chelmsford Cathedral
text: Chelmsford Cathedral in the city of Chelmsford, Essex, England, is dedicated to St Mary the Virgin, St Peter and St Cedd.

title: Chelmsford Cathedral
text: It became a cathedral when the Anglican Diocese of Chelmsford was created in 1914 and is the seat of the Bishop of Chelmsford.

title: Chennai International Airport
text: Chennai International Airport (IATA: MAA, ICAO: VOMM) is an international airport serving the city of Chennai (Madras), Tamil Nadu, India and its metropolitan area.

title: Chennai International Airport
text: It is the fourth busiest airport in India in terms of total passenger traffic after airports at Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru.

title: Chennai International Airport
text: It is the 49th busiest airport in Asia for CY 2016.

title: Chennai International Airport
text: In the fiscal year 2016-17, the airport handled over 18.3 million passengers.

title: Chennai International Airport
text: Over 400 aircraft movements are handled by the airport per day.

title: Chennai International Airport
text: Third busiest Airport in terms of cargo handling in India.

title: Chennai International Airport
text: The planned extension of the terminals are about to start as the union government has told that Chennai might not get its new airport soon.

title: Chicago 13
text: Chicago 13 is the eleventh studio album by the American band Chicago, released in 1979.

title: Chicago 13
text: The follow-up to "Hot Streets", "Chicago 13" is often critically disfavored.

title: Chicago 13
text: This would be the band's final release that features lead guitarist Donnie Dacus, who had followed late, founding lead guitarist, Terry Kath.

title: Chicago 13
text: All band members would contribute to the songwriting (one of only two albums where this is the case, with the other being "Chicago VII").

title: Chin Peng
text: Chin Peng (), former OBE, (21 October 1924 – 16 September 2013) born Ong Boon Hua () was a long-time leader of the Malayan Communist Party (MCP).

title: Chin Peng
text: A determined anti-colonialist, he led the party's guerrilla insurgency in the Malayan Emergency, fighting against British and Commonwealth forces in an attempt to establish an independent communist state.

title: Chin Peng
text: After the MCP's defeat and subsequent Malayan independence, Chin waged a second campaign against Malaya and, after 1963, the new state of Malaysia in an attempt to replace its government with a communist one from exile, until signing the Peace Agreement of Hat Yai 1989 with the Malaysian government in 1989.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: The majority of Chinese nationals currently residing in Samoa are businessmen, labour workers and shopowners in the south western island nation of Samoa, and there are at least 30,000 people in Samoa who are of mixed Samoan and Chinese descent, although they are classified as ethnic Samoans in official census.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: Around the world, about 25% of all Samoans claim Chinese ancestry.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: Notable Chinese businesses include Frankie's Supermarket and Wholesale, Alan wholesale and Treasure Garden company as well as other small businesses and restaurants.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: An estimated 4000 tourists visit Samoa every year via Faleolo international airport.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: Nearly all Chinese nationals in Samoa reside within the Apia municipal area; neighbouring American Samoa, also has a small population of Chinese expatriates.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: Samoas Legislative Capital city of Apia signed a treaty on 31:08:2015 with a delegation from Shenzhen, China making the Legislative capital of Apia and The city of Shenzhen, Guangdong, China sister cities.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: The treaty will help bring Chinese tourists to boast Samoas growing Tourism industry and will also bring economic growth to Samoa also bringing stronger ties between the two cities.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: Shenzhen Airlines is also set to operate flights from Shenzhen International airport and Faleolo International Airport, Apia.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: The Chinese community in Samoa is growing and becoming economically strong.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: A new wave of Chinese migrants moving to Samoa are coming from the northern region, bringing their culture and languages with them.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: There are no Chinese schools in Samoa but an estimated 98.7% of Chinese expatriates and migrants send their children and youth to Robert Louis Stevenson School, Samoa which is a private school with an Australasian and Samoan curriculum, the tuition fee is WST700-845.

title: Chinese in Samoa
text: There is a primary campus located in the village of Lotopa, Faleata District and the secondary campus in the urban village of Tafaigata.

title: Chirality (manga)
text: Chirality (キラリティー , Kiraritī ) is a 4-volume yuri manga series written and illustrated by author Satoshi Urushihara.

title: Chirality (manga)
text: The manga was originally serialized in "Comic NORA" in 1995, and later published in three bound volumes, which was re-released into two bound volumes in 2003.

title: Chirality (manga)
text: In 1997 "Chirality" was licensed for released in North America by Central Park Media.

title: Chirality (manga)
text: It was originally published as 18 issues between March 1997 and August 1998, as well as being released into four bound volumes from 1997 to 2000.

title: Chirality (manga)
text: The art was also flipped so that it would read left to right which was not an uncommon practice for manga released in Western Hemisphere at the time.

title: Chloë Agnew
text: Chloë Alexandra Adele Emily Agnew (born 9 June 1989 in Dublin, Ireland) is an Irish singer and songwriter who is an original former member of the Celtic music group Celtic Woman, as well as its youngest member.

title: Chloë Agnew
text: She comes from Knocklyon, County Dublin where she lived with her mother Adele "Twink" King and younger sister, Naomi.

title: Chloë Agnew
text: She sings in English, Irish, Latin, Italian, and German.

title: Chloë Agnew
text: Agnew has a soprano vocal range.

title: Chris Moller
text: Chris Moller is a former CEO of the New Zealand Rugby Union and former deputy CEO of New Zealand's largest company, Fonterra.

title: Chris Moller
text: Moller has also worked as managing director for New Zealand Milk Products.

title: Chris Moller
text: He is currently on the IRB council and became CEO of the NZRFU in January 2003.

title: Chris Moller
text: On 2 April 2007 he announced that he would not be renewing his contract as CEO after the 2007 Rugby World Cup.

title: Chris Moller
text: His deputy Steve Tew, was appointed to the role late in 2007.

title: Christian Serrón
text: Christian Ariel Serrón Acosta (born November 17, 1994 ) is a Uruguayan professional footballer who plays as an attacking midfielder for Rampla Juniors in the Uruguayan Segunda División, on loan from River Plate.

title: Christopher de Haro
text: Christopher de Haro (in Portuguese, Cristóvão de Haro) was a Lisbon-based merchant of Flemish origin.

title: Christopher de Haro
text: As a financier and representative of the Fuggers he provided the financial backing to Ferdinand Magellan's 1519 voyage, the first circumnavigation around the world.

title: Chuck Colby
text: Chuck Colby is an electronics engineer and chief-inventor, founder and president of Colby Systems Corporation, a company that created the first DVR-based video surveillance systems but is also very notable as a pioneer in portable computing, being the first to market both DOS and Macintosh portable computers, as well as a remarkable number of other technological firsts.

title: Cilgerran Castle
text: Cilgerran Castle (Welsh: "Castell Cilgerran" ) is a 13th-century ruined castle located in Cilgerran, Pembrokeshire, Wales, near Cardigan.

title: Cilgerran Castle
text: The first castle on the site was thought to be built by Gerald of Windsor around 1110–1115, and it changed hands several times over the following century between English and Welsh forces.

title: Cilgerran Castle
text: In the hands of William Marshal, 2nd Earl of Pembroke, the construction of the stone castle began after 1223.

title: Cilgerran Castle
text: After passing through successive families, it was left to ruin and eventually abandoned by 1400.

title: Cilgerran Castle
text: The castle backs onto a cliff face, with the remaining ruins dating from the 13th century.

title: Cilgerran Castle
text: It was most heavily fortified where it faces inland, and includes a pair of drum towers rather than a central keep which remain.

title: Cilgerran Castle
text: It passed into the hands of the National Trust in 1938, who open it to the public.

title: Circus Diablo
text: Circus Diablo is an American rock band, formed in early 2006 by Billy Morrison (vocals), Billy Duffy (lead guitar) and Ricky Warwick (rhythm guitar).

title: Circus Diablo
text: Fuel frontman Brett Scallions and Velvet Revolver drummer Matt Sorum subsequently joined the band on bass and drums, respectively.

title: Circus Diablo
text: To date, Circus Diablo have released one studio album, entitled "Circus Diablo".

title: Cirque du Soleil: Fire Within
text: Cirque du Soleil: Fire Within is a 2002 Canadian reality television mini-series.

title: Cirque du Soleil: Fire Within
text: The series follows eight Cirque du Soleil performers during the creation and production of the Cirque's touring production, "Varekai".

title: Cirque du Soleil: Fire Within
text: Stress ensues as several newcomers try to learn new acrobatic acts for the show, while the subplot also follows the crew behind the show trying to cast new performers, advertise the production, create the stage set, costumes, and make-up, and manage the show under the direction of newcomer Dominic Champagne.

title: Cirque du Soleil: Worlds Away
text: Cirque du Soleil: Worlds Away is a 2012 American 3D family fantasy film directed by Andrew Adamson.

title: Cirque du Soleil: Worlds Away
text: The film premiered on October 20, 2012 at the Tokyo International Film Festival, and was released theatrically in the United States on December 21, 2012.

title: Cirque du Soleil: Worlds Away
text: Distributed worldwide by Paramount Pictures on December 21, 2012, the film tells the story of a girl named Mia going to a traveling circus and falling in love with its main attraction, the Aerialist.

title: Cirque du Soleil: Worlds Away
text: After the Aerialist falls during his act, he and Mia are transported to another world where each encounter the different worlds of Cirque du Soleil through O, Mystère, Kà, Love, Zumanity, Viva Elvis and Criss Angel Believe.

title: Cirque du Soleil: Worlds Away
text: It stars Erica Linz and Igor Zaripov as the main characters and incorporates acts from some of the Cirque du Soleil shows that were running in Las Vegas in 2011 including O, Mystère, Kà, Love, and Viva Elvis.

title: Cirsium
text: Cirsium is a genus of perennial and biennial flowering plants in the Asteraceae, one of several genera known commonly as thistles.

title: Cirsium
text: They are more precisely known as plume thistles.

title: Cirsium
text: These differ from other thistle genera ("Carduus", "Silybum" and "Onopordum") in having feathered hairs to their achenes.

title: Cirsium
text: The other genera have a pappus of simple unbranched hairs.

title: City of Blacktown
text: Blacktown City is a local government area in western Sydney, situated on the Cumberland Plain, approximately 35 km west of the Sydney central business district, in the state of New South Wales, Australia.

title: City of Blacktown
text: The City occupies an area of 246.9 km2 and had a population of 336,962 as at the 2016 census .

title: Classic Brit Awards
text: The Classic BRIT Awards (previously Classical BRIT Awards) are an annual awards ceremony held in the United Kingdom covering aspects of classical and crossover music, and are the equivalent of pop music's Brit Awards.

title: Clean Bandit discography
text: English electronic music group Clean Bandit have released one studio album, three extended plays, seven singles (including one as a featured artist) and eleven music videos.

title: Clean Bandit discography
text: In December 2012, the group released their debut single "A+E", which peaked at number 100 on the UK Singles Chart.

title: Clean Bandit discography
text: The song is the lead single from their debut album, "New Eyes", which was released in May 2014.

title: Clean Bandit discography
text: The album's second single, "Mozart's House", charted at number seventeen on the UK Singles Chart, becoming Clean Bandit's first top twenty single on the chart. "

title: Clean Bandit discography
text: Dust Clears" was released as the third single from the album, reaching number forty-three on the UK chart.

title: Clean Bandit discography
text: The album's fourth single, "Rather Be", features Jess Glynne and topped the UK Singles Chart, the group's first number one on the chart.

title: Clean Bandit discography
text: Their 2016 single "Rockabye", which features rapper Sean Paul and singer Anne-Marie, became their second number-one hit in the UK, becoming the Christmas number one single for 2016 in its seventh consecutive week at number-one.

title: Clean Bandit discography
text: The follow-up to "Rockabye", "Symphony", featured Zara Larsson and became their third UK number one single.

title: Clement G. Morgan
text: Clement Garnett Morgan (1859-1929) was an American attorney, civil rights activist, and city official of Cambridge, Massachusetts.

title: Clement G. Morgan
text: Born into slavery in Virginia and freed by the Emancipation Proclamation, he trained as a barber before moving to Massachusetts to pursue his education.

title: Clement G. Morgan
text: He was the first African American to earn degrees from both Harvard University and its law school; the first African American to deliver Harvard's senior class oration; and the first black alderman in New England.

title: Clement G. Morgan
text: As an attorney he handled many civil rights cases, in one instance closing down a segregated school.

title: Clement G. Morgan
text: He was a founding member of the Niagara Movement and of the Boston branch of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People.

title: Cleomaceae
text: The Cleomaceae are a small family of flowering plants in the order Brassicales, comprising about 300 species in 10 genera, or about 150 species in 17 genera.

title: Cleomaceae
text: These genera were previously included in the family Capparaceae, but were raised to a distinct family when DNA evidence suggested the genera included in it are more closely related to the Brassicaceae than they are to the Capparaceae.

title: Cleomaceae
text: The APG II system allows for Cleomaceae to be included in Brassicaceae.

title: Cleveland Thyagaraja Festival
text: The Cleveland Thyagaraja Festival is a 12-day festival of South Indian classical music and dance in Cleveland, Ohio, and is held each year around Easter weekend.

title: Cleveland Thyagaraja Festival
text: The festival is a celebration in honor of Tyagaraja, the famous composer of Carnatic music, who composed thousands of devotional compositions, most in Telugu language .

title: Cleveland Thyagaraja Festival
text: The festival began in 1978, and has since grown to become the largest South Indian classical music and dance festival outside of India.

title: Cleveland Thyagaraja Festival
text: The festival draws its audience from all over the United States, as well as from Canada and other parts of the world.

title: Climax Golden Twins
text: Climax Golden Twins is an American experimental music band, formed in 1993 in Seattle, Washington by Robert Millis and Jeffery Taylor.

title: Climax Golden Twins
text: Scott Colburn joined in 1996 and left in 2004.

title: Climax Golden Twins
text: The group notably performed the soundtrack to the 2001 cult horror film "Session 9".

title: Climax Golden Twins
text: Other members have included Dave Abramson and John Vallier.

title: Climax Golden Twins
text: Millis and Taylor created the book Victrola Favorites: Artifacts From Bygone Days (Dust-to-Digital, 2008) which documented their respective 78rpm collections and have also worked with members of A_Frames as AFCGT releasing several LPs including the self-titled AFCGT on Subpop.

title: Climax Golden Twins
text: Messenger Girls Trio is another related project that features Millis, Taylor, Dave Knott and Sir Richard Bishop that has produced two LPs of improvised collaged acoustic guitar music.

title: Climbing!
text: Climbing!

title: Climbing!
text: , also known as Mountain Climbing!

title: Climbing!
text: Released on March 7, 1970, the album featured the 'classic' Mountain lineup of Leslie West (guitar, vocals), Felix Pappalardi (bass, vocals, piano), Corky Laing (drums, percussion) and Steve Knight (keyboards) and followed the West solo album "Mountain" featuring Pappalardi and drummer Norman Smart, released in 1969 and often credited to the band.

title: Climbing!

title: Climbing!

title: Climbing!
text: It was subsequently recorded and retitled for the album.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: Coimbatore International Airport (IATA: CJB, ICAO: VOCB) is the primary airport serving the city of Coimbatore in Tamil Nadu.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: It is located at Peelamedu, about 13 km from the center of the city.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: Previously known as Peelamedu Civil Aerodrome, it is the 19th busiest airport in India in terms of passengers handled, 16th busiest in terms of total aircraft movement and 14th busiest in terms of cargo handled.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: The airport is the second largest airport in terms of passenger traffic and cargo after Chennai International Airport In Tamil Nadu.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: About five domestic and three international airlines serve the airport.

title: Coimbatore International Airport
text: The Airport also serves as a growing hub for Cargo transportation.

title: Colocasia
text: Colocasia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Araceae, native to southeastern Asia and the Indian subcontinent.

title: Colocasia
text: Some species are widely cultivated and naturalized in other tropical and subtropical regions.

title: Colocasia
text: Common names include tarul, karkala ko ganu, elephant-ear, taro, cocoyam, dasheen, chembu, champadhumpa, shavige gadde, and eddoe.

title: Colocasia
text: Elephant-ear and cocoyam are also used for some other large-leaved genera in the Araceae, notably "Xanthosoma" and "Caladium".

title: Colocasia
text: The generic name is derived from the ancient Greek word "kolokasion", which in the Greek botanist Dioscorides (1st century AD) meant the edible roots of both "Colocasia esculenta" and "Nelumbo nucifera".

title: Colocasia
text: It is thought that the edible roots of "Colocasia esculenta" have been cultivated in Asia for more than ten thousand years.

title: Colocasia
text: The species "Colocasia esculenta" is an invasive species in wetlands along the American Gulf coast, where it threatens to displace native wetland plants.

title: Colonial Secretary of Tasmania
text: The Colonial Secretary of Van Diemen's Land (later Colonial Secretary of Tasmania) was the representative of the British Colonial Office in Van Diemen's Land (later Tasmania), and was usually appointed from Britain.

title: Colonial Times
text: The Colonial Times was a newspaper in Tasmania, Australia.

title: Colonial Times
text: It was established as the Colonial Times, and Tasmanian Advertiser in 1825 in Hobart, Van Diemen's Land (known as Tasmania since 1856) by the former editor of the "Hobart Town Gazette, and Van Diemen's Land Advertiser", Andrew Bent.

title: Colonial Times
text: The name was changed to "Colonial Times" in 1827, and the title was eventually absorbed into the "Hobart Town Mercury" in 1857.

title: Colorado Rockies
text: The Colorado Rockies are an American professional baseball team based in Denver, Colorado.

title: Colorado Rockies
text: The Rockies compete in Major League Baseball (MLB) as a member club of the National League (NL) West division.

title: Colorado Rockies
text: The team's home venue is Coors Field, located in the Lower Downtown area of Denver.

title: Colorado Rockies
text: The Rockies won their only National League championship in 2007, after having won 14 of their final 15 games in order to secure a Wild Card position.

title: Colorado Rockies
text: In the World Series they were swept by the American League (AL) champion Boston Red Sox in four games.

title: Colorado Rockies
text: They are one of two MLB franchises to have never won a division title (the other team is the Miami Marlins).

title: Commelinaceae
text: Commelinaceae is a family of flowering plants.

title: Commelinaceae
text: In less formal contexts, the group is referred to as the dayflower family or spiderwort family.

title: Commelinaceae
text: It is one of five families in the order Commelinales and by far the largest of these with about 731 known species in 41 genera.

title: Commelinaceae
text: Well known genera include "Commelina" (dayflowers) and "Tradescantia" (spiderworts).

title: Commelinaceae
text: The family is diverse in both the Old World tropics and the New World tropics, with some genera present in both.

title: Commelinaceae
text: The variation in morphology, especially that of the flower and inflorescence, is considered to be exceptionally high amongst the angiosperms.

title: Commelineae
text: Commelineae is a tribe of monocotyledonous flowering plants in the dayflower family (Commelinaceae).

title: Commelineae
text: The tribe consists of 13 genera and about 350 species.

title: Commelineae
text: It is one of two tribes in the subfamily Commelinoideae, the other being the Tradescantieae, which is made up of 26 genera and about 300 species.

title: Commelineae
text: The remaining two genera in the family are in a separate subfamily, the Cartonematoideae.

title: Commelinoideae
text: Commelinoideae is a subfamily of monocotyledonous flowering plants in the dayflower family (Commelinaceae).

title: Commelinoideae
text: The Commelinoideae is one of two subfamilies within the Commelinaceae and includes 39 genera (out of 41 in the family) and all but 12 of the family's several hundred known species.

title: Commelinoideae
text: The subfamily is further broken down into two tribes, the Tradescantieae, which includes 26 genera and about 300 species, and the Commelineae, which contains 13 genera and about 350 species.

title: Composer laureate
text: A composer laureate is a position awarded by a government as an honor to a musical composer.

title: Concealed shoes
text: Concealed shoes hidden in the fabric of a building have been discovered in many European countries, as well as in other parts of the world, since at least the early modern period.

title: Concealed shoes
text: Independent researcher Brian Hoggard has observed that the locations in which these shoes are typically found – in chimneys, under floors, above ceilings, around doors and windows, in the roof – suggest that some may have been concealed as magical charms to protect the occupants of the building against evil influences such as demons, ghosts and witches.

title: Concealed shoes
text: Others may have been intended to bestow fertility on a female member of the household, or been an offering to a household deity.

title: Conch Republic
text: The Conch Republic is a micronation declared as a tongue-in-cheek secession of the city of Key West, Florida, from the United States on April 23, 1982.

title: Conch Republic
text: It has been maintained as a tourism booster for the city since.

title: Conch Republic
text: Since then, the term "Conch Republic" has been expanded to refer to "all of the Florida Keys, or, that geographic apportionment of land that falls within the legally defined boundaries of Monroe County, Florida, northward to 'Skeeter's Last Chance Saloon' in Florida City, Dade County, Florida, with Key West as the nation's capital and all territories north of Key West being referred to as 'The Northern Territories'.

title: Consider the Source (web series)
text: Consider the Source is a 2015 Canadian-American web series directed by Brent Hodge and produced by Morgan Spurlock, produced through Spurlock's company Warrior Poets, Hodgee Films and Disney's Maker Studios.

title: Consider the Source (web series)
text: "Consider the Source" examines the everyday consumer products used by the public, such as gas or water, and the journeys that those products take to get from the factories and fields to store shelves and homes.

title: Consider the Source (web series)
text: The series was released on the YouTube channel "SMARTish".

title: Cordyline rubra
text: Cordyline rubra, known as the Palm Lily is an evergreen Australian plant.

title: Cordyline rubra
text: It grows as a shrub to around 4 metres (13 ft) tall.

title: Cordyline rubra
text: Found in warm rainforest and moist eucalyptus forest.

title: Cordyline rubra
text: The range of natural distribution is from Lismore to near Bundaberg, Queensland.

title: Corocoro United Copper Mines
text: The Corocoro United Copper Mines, Ltd. was the largest copper mine in Bolivia, an honor previously held by Compania Corocoro de Bolivia.

title: Corocoro United Copper Mines
text: The corporate office was at 151 Finsbury Pavement House, London, England, while the mine office was at Coro Coro, Bolivia.

title: Corocoro United Copper Mines
text: It was organized August 6, 1909 under the laws of Great Britain.

title: Corocoro United Copper Mines
text: The lands included 515 claims in the Coro Coro district.

title: Corocoro United Copper Mines
text: The principal mines were the Wisk'achani, formerly owned by J. K. Child & Co., Ltd.; the Santa Rosa, formerly owned by Carreras Hermanos; and the Guallatiri, formerly owned by the Succession Noel Berthin.

title: Corocoro United Copper Mines
text: The mines were opened on two successive conglomerate strata of different geological horizons, and similar only in their origin and cupriferous nature.

title: Corocoro United Copper Mines
text: The mines are believed to have been worked by the Incas.

title: Corocoro United Copper Mines
text: The nearest water supply was the Rio Desaguadero, 14 miles away, down which the copper was shipped by way of Puerto de Desaguadero, and from there to Mollendo, Chile, for export to Europe.

title: Coronilla
text: The genus Coronilla contains about 20 species of flowering plants native to Europe and North Africa.

title: Council of Orange (529)
text: The Second Council of Orange (or Second Synod of Orange) was held in 529 at Orange, which was then part of the Ostrogothic Kingdom.

title: Council of Orange (529)
text: It affirmed much of the theology of Augustine of Hippo, and made numerous proclamations against what later would come to be known as semi-Pelagian doctrine.

title: Country Grammar
text: Country Grammar is the debut studio album by American rapper Nelly.

title: Country Grammar
text: It was released on June 27, 2000, by Universal Records (who released the album after listening to demos by Nelly, before signing a record deal with the rapper in 1999).

title: Country Grammar
text: The production on the album was handled by Jason "Jay E" Epperson, with additional production by C-Love, Kevin Law, City Spud, Steve "Blast" Wills and Basement Beats.

title: Country Grammar
text: Nelly contributed to all lyrics on the album, with Epperson and City Spud also contributing.

title: Country Grammar
text: The album introduced a unique Saint Louis, Midwestern sound, and introduces Nelly's vocal style of pop-rap singalongs and Midwestern, Missouri twang.

title: Country Grammar
text: It was supported four successful singles: "Country Grammar (Hot Shit)", "E.I.", "Ride wit Me" and "Batter Up".

title: Country Grammar
text: Its lead single, "Country Grammar (Hot Shit)", peaked at number 7 on the "Billboard" Hot 100 and UK Singles Chart.

title: Country Grammar
text: "E.I." charted at number 16, number 12 and number 11 on the Hot 100, UK Singles Chart and ARIA Singles Chart, respectively.

title: Country Grammar
text: "Ride wit Me" peaked within the top five on the Hot 100, ARIA Singles Chart, Irish Singles Chart and UK Singles Chart.

title: Country Grammar
text: The album's fourth and final single, "Batter Up" featuring Murphy Lee and Ali, achieved moderate chart success.

title: Couplet
text: A couplet is a pair of successive lines of metre in poetry.

title: Couplet
text: A couplet usually consists of two successive lines that rhyme and have the same metre.

title: Couplet
text: A couplet may be formal (closed) or run-on (open).

title: Couplet
text: In a formal (or closed) couplet, each of the two lines is end-stopped, implying that there is a grammatical pause at the end of a line of verse.

title: Couplet
text: In a run-on (or open) couplet, the meaning of the first line continues to the second.

title: Craig Virgin
text: Craig Steven Virgin (born August 2, 1955) is an American distance runner.

title: Craig Virgin
text: He was born in Belleville, Illinois and grew up near Lebanon, Illinois.

title: Craig Virgin
text: While in high school, Virgin won 5 state championships (two in cross country and three in track) as well as setting the national outdoor high school 2-mile record of 8:40.9 (beating Steve Prefontaine's mark of 8:41.5, though slightly short of Gerry Lindgren's 8:40.0 indoor record from 1964).

title: Craig Virgin
text: Additionally, Virgin remains the record-holder in Illinois Boys Cross Country, running a 13:50.6 in 1972, which has only been approached by within five seconds by Chris Derrick in 2007 (13:51.8) and Lukas Verzbicas in 2010 (13:53.8).

title: Craig Virgin
text: He was "Track and Field News" "High School Athlete of the Year" in 1973.

title: Craig Wedren
text: Following the disbandment of Shudder to Think, Wedren pursued a career as a television and film music composer, as well as releasing solo material.

title: Cress Williams

title: Cress Williams

title: Cross country running
text: Cross country running is a sport in which teams and individuals run a race on open-air courses over natural terrain such as dirt or grass.

title: Cross country running
text: Sometimes the runners are referred to as "harriers" (dogs).

title: Cross country running
text: The course, typically 4 - long, may include surfaces of grass, and earth, pass through woodlands and open country, and include hills, flat ground and sometimes gravel road.

title: Cross country running
text: It is both an individual and a team sport; runners are judged on individual times and teams by a points-scoring method.

title: Cross country running
text: Both men and women of all ages compete in cross country, which usually takes place during autumn and winter, and can include weather conditions of rain, sleet, snow or hail, and a wide range of temperatures.

title: Croydon Airport
text: The terminal building and entrance lodge are Grade II listed buildings.

title: Cyclone Oswald
text: Tropical Cyclone Oswald in January 2013 passed over parts of Queensland and New South Wales, Australia over a number of days, causing widespread impact including severe storms, flooding, and water spouts. Coastal regions of Queensland were the most impacted with Mundubbera, Eidsvold, Gayndah and Bundaberg in the Wide Bay–Burnett hit severely.

title: Cyclone Oswald
text: In many places the rainfall total for January set new records.

title: Cyclone Oswald
text: Across the affected region, damage from severe weather and flooding amounted to at least A$2.4 billion (US$2.5 billion).

title: Daniel J. Miller
text: Colonel Daniel J. Miller was born in Stony Point, New York.

title: Daniel J. Miller
text: He enlisted in the United States Army Air Forces during World War II and served in the 826th Bombardment Squadron as a navigator in a B-24 Liberator.

title: Daniel J. Miller
text: During the Korean War, he flew various aircraft, including the F-86 Sabre jet fighter.

title: Daniel J. Miller
text: In the late Korean War and throughout the Vietnam War, he flew helicopter rescue missions.

title: Daniel J. Miller
text: He was awarded the Silver Star during the Korean War in the 3rd Rescue Squadron.

title: Daniel J. Miller
text: He braved heavy enemy fire in low visibility to rescue USMC Major Frank H. Presley.

title: Daniel J. Miller
text: Immediately after rescuing Presley, his P-51 fighter escort was shot down, and he once again braved the fire to attempt to rescue USAF Captain Willis R. Brown, but Brown had failed to eject and had perished.

title: Daniel J. Miller
text: In addition, he was also awarded the Cheney Award for a rescue in February 1951, when he rescued six wounded soldiers behind enemy lines in three attempts despite snow and enemy fire.

title: Daniel J. Miller
text: During Vietnam, he flew rescue missions and commanded a light reconnaissance squadron, the 19th Tactical Air Support Squadron.

title: Del Monte Center

title: Delmar, Alabama

title: Democratic Party (South Africa)
text: The Democratic Party (DP) was the name of the South African political party now called the Democratic Alliance.

title: Democratic Party (South Africa, 1973)
text: The party hoped to be a rallying point for the "verligte" (enlightened) Nationalists who had grown disillusioned with the hardline apartheid government of John Vorster and attracted support from younger Afrikaners.

title: Democratic Party (South Africa, 1973)

title: Dictyosperma
text: Dictyosperma is a monotypic genus of flowering plant in the palm family found in the Mascarene Islands in the Indian Ocean (Mauritius, Réunion and Rodrigues).

title: Dictyosperma
text: The sole species, Dictyosperma album, is widely cultivated in the tropics but has been farmed to near extinction in its native habitat.

title: Dictyosperma
text: It is commonly called princess palm or hurricane palm, the latter owing to its ability to withstand strong winds by easily shedding leaves.

title: Dictyosperma
text: It is closely related to, and resembles, palms in the "Archontophoenix" genus.

title: Dictyosperma
text: The genus is named from two Greek words meaning "net" and "seed" and the epithet is Latin for "white", the common color of the crownshaft at the top of the trunk.

title: Dysosmia
text: Dysosmia is a disorder described as any qualitative alteration or distortion of the perception of smell.

title: Dysosmia
text: Qualitative alterations differ from quantitative alterations, which include anosmia and hyposmia.

title: Dysosmia
text: Dysosmia can be classified as either parosmia (also called troposmia) or phantosmia.

title: Dysosmia
text: Parosmia refers to a distortion in the perception of an odorant.

title: Dysosmia
text: Odorants smell different from what one remembers.

title: Dysosmia
text: Phantosmia refers to the perception of an odor when there's no actual odorant present.

title: Dysosmia
text: The cause of dysosmia still remains a theory.

title: Dysosmia
text: It is typically considered a neurological disorder and clinical associations with the disorder have been made.

title: Dysosmia
text: Most cases are described as idiopathic and the main antecedents related to parosmia are URTIs, head trauma, and nasal and paranasal sinus disease.

title: Dysosmia
text: Dysosmia tends to go away on its own but there are options for treatment for patients that want immediate relief.

title: East Walnut Hills, Cincinnati
text: East Walnut Hills is a neighborhood in Cincinnati, Ohio, United States.

title: East Walnut Hills, Cincinnati
text: Founded in 1867, originally as the independent incorporated village of Woodburn, East Walnut Hills is a diverse neighborhood, both ethnically and economically.

title: East Walnut Hills, Cincinnati
text: It has long been known as a very fashionable neighborhood and home to many prominent Cincinnatians.

title: East Walnut Hills, Cincinnati
text: The neighborhood includes the large historic district between the O'Bryonville business district (Evanston) and the DeSales Corner (East Walnut Hills), home to opulent mansions with large setbacks, as well as Annwood Park on Madison Road and the Bettman Preserve, an urban nature preserve.

title: East Walnut Hills, Cincinnati

title: East Walnut Hills, Cincinnati

title: East Windsor Hill Historic District

title: Elemund
text: Elemund (Latin: "Elemundus", died 548) was king of the Gepids, an east Germanic people, during the first half of the 6th century.

title: Elemund
text: He may have ascended by overthrowing the Ardariking dynasty, the line of Gepid kings descended from king Ardaric.

title: Elemund
text: Basing himself on archaeological evidence, István Boná believes that in the 520s or 530s Elemund must have consolidated his power in Transylvania by submitting or removing minor Gepid rulers.

title: Elemund
text: Elemund had a son and daughter, Ostrogotha and Austrigusa respectively; the latter was given in marriage to Wacho, the king of the Lombards, in 512.

title: Elemund
text: The reasons behind the marriage were multiple: on one side it protected the two kings from the threat represented by the Ostrogothic Kingdom, while on the other it reduced the danger represented to the Lombard king by Ildechis, a pretender to the Lombard throne.

title: Elemund
text: Wacho was eventually to remarry after Austrigusa's death, but this did not compromise the good relations existing between Lombards and Gepids.

title: Elemund
text: Elemund died of illness in 548 and was succeeded by Thurisind, while the legitimate heir was forced into exile.

title: Elemund
text: Ostrogotha found hospitality among the Lombards, but was to be killed in 552 by his host, King Audoin, as part of a plan to ease relations among Gepids and Lombards.

title: Elephant

title: Emergency Action Message
text: In the U.S. military's strategic nuclear weapon nuclear command and control (NC2) system, an Emergency Action Message (EAM) is a preformatted message that directs nuclear-capable forces to execute specific Major Attack Options (MAOs) or Limited Attack Options (LAOs) in a nuclear war.

title: Emergency Action Message
text: Individual countries or specific regions may be included or withheld in the EAM, as specified in the Single Integrated Operational Plan (SIOP).

title: Emergency Action Message
text: The SIOP was updated annually until February 2003, when it was replaced by Operations Plan (OPLAN) 8044.

title: Emergency Action Message
text: Since July 2012, the US nuclear war plan has been OPLAN 8010-12, "Strategic Deterrence and Force Employment".

title: Ender Wiggin

title: Ender in Exile
text: Ender in Exile is a science fiction novel by Orson Scott Card, part of the "Ender's Game" series, published on November 11, 2008.

title: Ender in Exile
text: It takes place between the two award-winning novels: "Ender's Game" and "Speaker for the Dead".

title: Ender in Exile
text: It could also be considered a parallel novel to the first three sequels in the Shadow Saga, since the entirety of this "trilogy" takes place in the span of "Ender in Exile".

title: Ender in Exile
text: The novel concludes a dangling story line of the Shadow Saga, while it makes several references to events that take place during the Shadow Saga.

title: Ender in Exile
text: From yet another perspective, the novel expands (or "replaces") the last chapter of the original novel "Ender's Game".

title: Ender in Exile
text: On the one hand, it fills the gap right before the last chapter, and on the other hand, it fills the gap between the last chapter and the original (first) sequel (both named "Speaker for the Dead").

title: Ender in Exile
text: "Ender in Exile" begins one year after Ender has won the bugger war, and begins with the short story "Ender's Homecoming" from Card's webzine Intergalactic Medicine Show.

title: Ender in Exile
text: Other short stories that were published elsewhere are included as chapters of the novel.

title: English trust law
text: English trust law concerns the creation and protection of asset funds, which are usually held by one party for another's benefit.

title: English trust law
text: Trusts were a creation of the English law of property and obligations, but also share a history with countries across the Commonwealth and the United States.

title: English trust law
text: Trusts developed when claimants in property disputes were dissatisfied with the common law courts and petitioned the King for a just and equitable result.

title: English trust law
text: On the King's behalf, the Lord Chancellor developed a parallel justice system in the Court of Chancery.

title: English trust law
text: Historically, trusts were mostly used where people left money in a will, created family settlements, created charities, or some types of business venture.

title: English trust law
text: After the Judicature Act 1873, England's courts of equity and common law were merged, and equitable principles took precedence.

title: English trust law
text: Today, trusts play an important role in financial investments, especially in unit trusts and pension trusts, where trustees and fund managers usually invest assets for people who wish to save for retirement.

title: English trust law
text: Although people are generally free to write trusts in any way they like, an increasing number of statutes are designed to protect beneficiaries, or regulate the trust relationship, including the Trustee Act 1925, Trustee Investments Act 1961, Recognition of Trusts Act 1987, Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, Trustee Act 2000, Pensions Act 1995, Pensions Act 2004 and the Charities Act 2011.

title: Enkidu
text: Enkidu ( EN.KI.DU, "Enki's creation") is a central figure in the Ancient Mesopotamian "Epic of Gilgamesh".

title: Enkidu
text: Enkidu was formed from clay and saliva by Aruru, the goddess of creation, to rid Gilgamesh of his arrogance.

title: Enkidu
text: In the story he is a wild man, raised by animals and ignorant of human society until he is bedded by Shamhat.

title: Enkidu
text: Thereafter a series of interactions with humans and human ways bring him closer to civilization, culminating in a wrestling match with Gilgamesh, king of Uruk.

title: Enkidu
text: Enkidu embodies the wild or natural world.

title: Enkidu
text: Though equal to Gilgamesh in strength and bearing, he acts in some ways as an antithesis to the cultured, urban-bred warrior-king.

title: Enkidu
text: Enkidu then becomes the king's constant companion and deeply beloved friend, accompanying him on adventures until he is stricken with illness and dies.

title: Enkidu
text: The deep, tragic loss of Enkidu profoundly inspires in Gilgamesh a quest to escape death by obtaining godly immortality.

title: Epic of Gilgamesh
text: The Epic of Gilgamesh is an epic poem from ancient Mesopotamia that is often regarded as the earliest surviving great work of literature.

title: Epic of Gilgamesh
text: The literary history of Gilgamesh begins with five Sumerian poems about 'Bilgamesh' (Sumerian for 'Gilgamesh'), king of Uruk, dating from the Third Dynasty of Ur (circa 2100 BC).

title: Epic of Gilgamesh
text: These independent stories were later used as source material for a combined epic.

title: Epic of Gilgamesh
text: The first surviving version of this combined epic, known as the "Old Babylonian" version, dates to the 18th century BC and is titled after its "incipit", Shūtur eli sharrī ("Surpassing All Other Kings").

title: Epic of Gilgamesh
text: Only a few tablets of it have survived.

title: Epic of Gilgamesh
text: The later "Standard" version dates from the 13th to the 10th centuries BC and bears the "incipit" Sha naqba īmuru ("He who Saw the Deep", in modern terms: "He who Sees the Unknown").

title: Epic of Gilgamesh
text: Approximately two thirds of this longer, twelve-tablet version have been recovered.

title: Epic of Gilgamesh
text: Some of the best copies were discovered in the library ruins of the 7th-century BC Assyrian king Ashurbanipal.

title: Ernest McBride, Sr.
text: Ernest Samuel McBride, Sr (November 20, 1909 – May 5, 2007) was an African American civil rights activist and community leader based in Long Beach, California.

title: Ernest McBride, Sr.
text: He fought to improve the working prospects and conditions of African Americans in the shipyards, grocery stores, housing, police and fire departments in Long Beach.

title: Ernest McBride, Sr.
text: He was a co-founder of the Long Beach chapter of National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP).

title: Ernest McBride, Sr.
text: Like Martin Luther King, Jr., McBride employed Mahatma Gandhi's model of peaceful protest to achieve civil rights gains.

title: Ernest McBride, Sr.

title: Ernest McBride, Sr.
text: McBride's legacy is memorialized in numerous awards, historic land marking of his home, and the naming of a high school and park.

title: Ernestine Cannon

title: Ernestine Cannon

title: Ernestine Cannon

title: Ernestine Cannon

title: Escape and evasion map
text: Evasion charts, are maps made for servicemembers to be used when caught behind enemy lines to perform escape and evasion, escape maps were secreted to prisoners of war by various means to aid in escape attempts.

title: Escape and evasion map
text: During World War II, these maps were used by many American, British, and allied servicemen to escape from behind enemy lines.

title: Escape and evasion map

title: Five-planet Nice model
text: The five-planet Nice model is a recent variation of the Nice model that begins with five giant planets, the current four plus an additional ice giant, in a chain of mean-motion resonances.

title: Five-planet Nice model

title: Geometric standard deviation
text: In probability theory and statistics, the geometric standard deviation describes how spread out are a set of numbers whose preferred average is the geometric mean.

title: Geometric standard deviation
text: For such data, it may be preferred to the more usual standard deviation.

title: Geometric standard deviation
text: Note that unlike the usual "arithmetic" standard deviation, the "geometric" standard deviation is a multiplicative factor, and thus is dimensionless, rather than having the same dimension as the input values.

title: Geometric standard deviation
text: Thus, the geometric standard deviation may be more appropriately called geometric SD factor [1, 2].

title: Geometric standard deviation
text: When using geometric SD factor in conjunction with geometric mean, it should be described as "the range from (the geometric mean divided by the geometric SD factor) to (the geometric mean multiplied by the geometric SD factor", and one cannot add/subtract "geometric SD factor" to/from geometric mean [3].

title: Halloween on Franklin Street
text: Halloween on Franklin Street is a yearly tradition in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, that encompasses a massive gathering on Franklin Street, the cultural hub of the town.

text: The Halloween celebration began in the early 1980s as a considerably smaller event, involving Chapel Hill residents and college students from The University of North Carolina.

title: Halloween on Franklin Street
text: In 2008, the Town of Chapel Hill implemented new measures to attempt to cut down on the size of the Halloween celebration in an action dubbed "Homegrown Halloween" to reduce the crowd size and discourage people from out of town to come to Chapel Hill.

title: Halloween on Franklin Street
text: The shuttle service that had formerly transported people from park and ride lots to Franklin Street was shut down and the results of Chapel Hill's efforts showed when about 35,000 people showed up for the event.

title: Halloween on Franklin Street
text: Attendees of the event dress up in creative Halloween costumes and walk up and down Franklin Street celebrating the holiday.

title: Halloween on Franklin Street
text: Since its beginnings, the event had grown in size every year until 2008.

title: Halloween on Franklin Street
text: Although not sponsored by the Town of Chapel Hill, the celebration has become an attraction for visitors from across the South.

title: Halloween on Franklin Street
text: Between 2004 and 2007, it was estimated that about 80,000 people converged on Franklin Street for the event, while Chapel Hill is estimated to have a population of 54,492 as listed in the 2007 census, evidence of the number of people who make the trip to Chapel Hill to attend.

title: Halloween on Franklin Street
text: Because of the size of the celebration, the Town of Chapel Hill closes Franklin Street to all vehicular traffic and prohibits parking anywhere near downtown.

title: Halloween on Franklin Street
text: Along with the big crowds come safety issues, with some of the biggest concerns being alcohol poisoning and gang-related violence.

title: Halloween on Franklin Street
text: To deal with these issues, hundreds of police officers patrol the downtown area throughout the entire night.

title: Halloween on Franklin Street

title: Heads up poker
text: Heads up poker is a form of poker that is played between only two players.

title: Heads up poker

title: Heisman curse
text: The Heisman curse is a term coined to reference a two-part assertion of a negative future for the winning player of the Heisman Trophy.

title: Heisman curse
text: The "curse" supposes that any college football player who wins the Heisman plays on a team that will likely lose its subsequent bowl game.

title: Heisman curse
text: The trend of post-award failure has garnered the attention of the mainstream media.

title: Heisman curse
text: Talk of a curse in relation to bowl results was particularly prevalent from 2003 to 2008, when six Heisman Trophy winners compiled a cumulative 1–5 bowl game record, and five of those six led number one ranked teams into the Bowl Championship Series (BCS) National Championship Game as favorites (Heisman Trophy winners, including Reggie Bush, who gave back his Heisman Trophy, are 4–8 overall in the BCS National Championship Game and College Football Playoff National Championship, although prior to 2009 they were 1–6).

title: Heisman curse
text: Additionally, the Heisman curse asserts that in most cases a Heisman winner will have either a poor career in the National Football League (NFL), or in fact not even see such a football career at all.

title: Heisman curse
text: Although many Heisman winners have not enjoyed success at the professional level, including players like Matt Leinart, Andre Ware, Jason White, Rashaan Salaam, Eric Crouch, Ty Detmer, Troy Smith and Gino Torretta, proponents of the "curse" rarely cite highly successful players such as Barry Sanders, Charles Woodson, Eddie George, Tim Brown, Bo Jackson, Marcus Allen, Earl Campbell, and Tony Dorsett among the notables.

title: Highland Inn

title: Highways Act 1980

title: History of laptops
text: The history of laptops describes the efforts in the 1970s and 1980s to build small, portable personal computers that combine the components, inputs, outputs and capabilities of a desktop computer in a small chassis.

title: History of laptops
text: Before laptop/notebook computers were technically feasible, similar ideas had been proposed, most notably Alan Kay's Dynabook concept, developed at Xerox PARC in the early 1970s.

title: History of laptops
text: One of the first reasonably portable computers was the Xerox NoteTaker, again developed at Xerox PARC, in 1976.

title: History of laptops

title: Hollywood Theater (Minneapolis)
text: The Hollywood Theater is a historic theater building in Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States, which is listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places.

title: Hollywood Theater (Minneapolis)
text: The Art Deco theater building opened on October 26, 1935, and the marquee proclaimed it the "Incomparable Showcase of the Northwest".

title: Hollywood Theater (Minneapolis)
text: The theater, designed by architects Jack Liebenberg and Seeman Kaplan, had a generous budget that allowed for elaborate decoration in the Streamline Deco style of design; its facade and structure made a "powerful statement of geometric mass punctuated by the entrance, exits, and three small windows that served the projection booth."

title: Hollywood Theater (Minneapolis)
text: Liebenberg and Kaplan went on to design the Riverview Theatre in Minneapolis and the Terrace Theatre in Robbinsdale.

title: Hollywood Theater (Minneapolis)
text: The building featured a tall vertical sign, a patterned terrazzo floor, gilded pillars, and acoustical tiles in geometric patterns.

title: Hollywood Theater (Minneapolis)
text: It had a seating capacity of just under 1000.

title: Hollywood Theater (Minneapolis)
text: Much of the interior features are influenced by the Zig-Zag Moderne and Streamline Moderne styles.

title: Hollywood Theater (Minneapolis)
text: The exterior is built of smooth Kasota limestone with vertical lines that transition to horizontal.

title: Homestead Extension of Florida's Turnpike
text: The Homestead Extension of Florida's Turnpike (HEFT), designated as State Road 821 (SR 821) and the Ronald Reagan Turnpike, is the southern extension of Florida's Turnpike, a toll road in Florida operated by Florida's Turnpike Enterprise (FTE).

title: Huernia
text: The genus Huernia (family Apocynaceae, subfamily Asclepiadoideae) consists of stem succulents from Eastern and Southern Africa, first described as a genus in 1810.

title: Huernia
text: The flowers are five-lobed, usually somewhat more funnel- or bell-shaped than in the closely related genus "Stapelia", and often striped vividly in contrasting colours or tones, some glossy, others matt and wrinkled depending on the species concerned.

title: Huernia
text: To pollinate, the flowers attract flies by emitting a scent similar to that of carrion.

title: Huernia
text: The genus is considered close to the genera "Stapelia" and "Hoodia".

title: Huernia
text: The name is in honour of Justin Heurnius (1587–1652) a Dutch missionary who is reputed to have been the first collector of South African Cape plants.

title: Huernia
text: His name was actually mis-spelt by the collector.

title: Human Biology (journal)
text: Human Biology is a peer reviewed scientific journal, currently published by Wayne State University Press.

title: Human Biology (journal)
text: The journal was established in 1929 by Raymond Pearl and is the official publication of the American Association of Anthropological Genetics.

title: Human Biology (journal)
text: The focus of the journal is human genetics, covering topics from human population genetics, evolutionary and genetic demography and quantitative genetics.

title: Human Biology (journal)
text: It also covers ancient DNA studies, evolutionary biological anthropology, and research exploring biological diversity expressed in terms of adaptation.

title: Human Biology (journal)
text: The journal also publishes interdisciplinary research linking biological and cultural diversity from evidence such sources as archaeology, ethnography and cultural anthropology studies, and more.

title: Human Biology (journal)
text: As of July 1, 2016, the journal is on Volume 87, Issue 3.

title: Human Biology (journal)
text: The journal's current editors are Brian M. Kemp (Washington State University) and Ripan S. Malhi (University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign).

title: Human Protein Atlas
text: The Human Protein Atlas (HPA) is a Swedish-based program started in 2003 with the aim to map of all the human proteins in cells, tissues and organs using integration of various omics technologies, including antibody-based imaging, mass spectrometry-based proteomics, transcriptomics and systems biology.

title: Human Protein Atlas
text: All the data in the knowledge resource is open access to allow scientists both in academia and industry to freely access the data for exploration of the human proteome.

title: Human Protein Atlas
text: The version 17 (launched August 17, 2017) consists of three separate parts, each focusing on a particular aspect of the genome-wide analysis of the human proteins; the Tissue Atlas showing the distribution of the proteins across all major tissues and organs in the human body, the Cell Atlas showing the subcellular localization of proteins in single cells, and finally the new Pathology Atlas showing the impact of protein levels for survival of patients with cancer.

title: Human Protein Atlas
text: The Human Protein Atlas program has already contributed to several thousands of publications in the field of human biology and disease and it was recently (July 25, 2017) selected by the organization ELIXIR as a European core resource due to its fundamental importance for a wider life science community.

title: Human Protein Atlas
text: The HPA consortium is funded by the Knut and Alice Wallenberg Foundation.

title: Human trafficking in Taiwan
text: Taiwan is primarily a destination for men, women, and children trafficked for the purposes of forced labor and sexual exploitation.

title: Human trafficking in Taiwan
text: It is also a source of women trafficked to Japan, Australia, the United Kingdom, and the United States.

title: Human trafficking in Taiwan
text: Women and girls from the People’s Republic of China (P.R.C.) and Southeast Asian countries are trafficked to Taiwan through fraudulent marriages, deceptive employment offers, and illegal smuggling for sexual exploitation and forced labor.

title: Human trafficking in Taiwan
text: Many trafficking victims are workers from rural areas of Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia, and the Philippines, employed through recruitment agencies and brokers to perform low skilled work in Taiwan’s construction, fishing, and manufacturing industries, or to work as domestic servants.

title: Human trafficking in Taiwan
text: Such workers are often charged high job placement and service fees, up to $14,000, resulting in substantial debt that labor brokers or employers use as a tool for involuntary servitude.

title: Human trafficking in Taiwan
text: Many foreign workers remain vulnerable to trafficking because legal protections, oversight by authorities and enforcement efforts are inadequate.

title: Human trafficking in Taiwan
text: Taiwan authorities reported that traffickers continued to use fraudulent marriages to facilitate labor and sex trafficking, despite increased efforts by the authorities to prevent this practice.

title: Human trafficking in Taiwan
text: Some women who are smuggled onto Taiwan to seek illegal work were sometimes sold in auctions to sex traffickers, and subsequently forced to work in the commercial sex industry.

title: Human trafficking in Taiwan
text: NGOs reported a sharp increase during the reporting period in the number of boys rescued from prostitution, mainly discovered during police investigations of online social networking sites suspected of being front operations for prostitution rings.

title: Husnlal Bhagatram
