title: Jumping-Jupiter scenario
text: The jumping-Jupiter scenario specifies an evolution of giant-planet migration described by the Nice model, in which an ice giant (Uranus, Neptune, or an additional Neptune-mass planet) is scattered inward by Saturn and outward by Jupiter, causing the step-wise separation of their orbits.

title: Jumping-Jupiter scenario
text: The jumping-Jupiter scenario was proposed by Ramon Brasser, Alessandro Morbidelli, Rodney Gomes, Kleomenis Tsiganis, and Harold Levison after their studies revealed that the smooth divergent migration of Jupiter and Saturn resulted in an inner Solar System significantly different from the current Solar System.

title: Jumping-Jupiter scenario
text: The sweeping of secular resonances through the inner Solar System during the migration excited the eccentricities of the terrestrial planets beyond current values and left an asteroid belt with an excessive ratio of high- to low-inclination objects.

title: Jumping-Jupiter scenario
text: The step-wise separation of Jupiter and Saturn described in the jumping-Jupiter scenario can allow these resonances to quickly cross the inner Solar System without altering orbits excessively, although the terrestrial planets remain sensitive to its passage.

title: Jumping-Jupiter scenario
text: The jumping-Jupiter scenario also results in a number of other differences with the original Nice model.

title: Jumping-Jupiter scenario
text: The fraction of lunar impactors from the core of the asteroid belt during the Late Heavy Bombardment is significantly reduced, most of the Jupiter trojans are captured during Jupiter's encounters with the ice giant, as are Jupiter's irregular satellites.

title: Jumping-Jupiter scenario
text: In the jumping-Jupiter scenario, the likelihood of preserving four giant planets on orbits resembling their current ones appears to increase if the early Solar System originally contained an additional ice giant, which was later ejected by Jupiter into interstellar space.

title: Jumping-Jupiter scenario
text: However, this remains an atypical result, as is the preservation of the current orbits of the terrestrial planets.

title: Kuiper belt
text: The Kuiper belt ( or ] ), sometimes called the Edgeworth–Kuiper belt, is a circumstellar disc in the Solar System beyond the (known) planets, extending from the orbit of Neptune (at 30 AU) to approximately 50 AU from the Sun.

title: Kuiper belt
text: It is similar to the asteroid belt, but is far larger—20 times as wide and 20 to 200 times as massive.

title: Kuiper belt
text: Like the asteroid belt, it consists mainly of small bodies or remnants from when the Solar System formed.

title: Kuiper belt
text: While many asteroids are composed primarily of rock and metal, most Kuiper belt objects are composed largely of frozen volatiles (termed "ices"), such as methane, ammonia and water.

title: Kuiper belt
text: The Kuiper belt is home to three officially recognized dwarf planets: Pluto, Haumea and Makemake.

title: Kuiper belt
text: Some of the Solar System's moons, such as Neptune's Triton and Saturn's Phoebe, are thought to have originated in the region.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: The Lakers–Clippers rivalry is a National Basketball Association (NBA) rivalry between the Los Angeles Lakers and Los Angeles Clippers.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: The two Pacific Division teams both play their home games at Staples Center in Los Angeles, inspiring their matchups to sometimes be called the "Hallway Series".

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: With the Clippers' 3-1 series win in 2016-17, the Lakers have now won the season series just four times in the past 13 seasons, with five Clippers wins, four Lakers wins, and four ties.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: The Lakers hold a 99–47 advantage in the all-time series against the Clippers.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: The two teams have never met in the playoffs.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: The Lakers relocated from Minneapolis in 1960, while the Clippers moved from San Diego in 1984.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: Los Angeles fans have historically favored the Lakers.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: But the Clippers have sold out every home game at Staples Center since Feb. 2011 and entered the 2016–17 season with the sixth-longest active sellout streak in the NBA.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: The Lakers have won 11 of their 16 NBA championships since moving to Los Angeles.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: Meanwhile, the Clippers have made the playoffs only nine times since 1984 and were long considered the laughingstock of the NBA; in the history of the franchise, they have never advanced past the second round of the playoffs.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: Some contended that the term "rivalry" was inaccurate until the Clippers became more successful.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: For the first time in 20 years, the Clippers won the season series against the Lakers in 2012–13.

title: Lakers–Clippers rivalry
text: This was the first of five straight season series victories for the Clippers, which included season sweeps in both 2014-15 and 2015-16.

title: List of hyperbolic comets
text: The following is a list of parabolic and hyperbolic comets in the Solar System.

title: List of hyperbolic comets
text: Many of these comets may come from the Oort cloud, or perhaps even have interstellar origin.

title: List of hyperbolic comets
text: The Oort Cloud is not gravitationally attracted enough to the Sun to form into a fairly thin disk, like the inner Solar System.

title: List of hyperbolic comets
text: Thus comets originating from the Oort Cloud can come from roughly any orientation (inclination to the ecliptic), and many even have a retrograde orbit.

title: List of hyperbolic comets
text: By definition, a hyperbolic orbit means that the comet will only travel through the Solar System once, with the Sun acting as a gravitational slingshot, sending the comet hurtling out of the Solar System entirely unless its eccentricity is otherwise changed.

title: List of hyperbolic comets
text: Comets orbiting in this way still originate from the Solar System, however.

title: List of hyperbolic comets
text: Typically comets in the Oort Cloud are thought to have roughly circular orbits around the Sun, but their orbital velocity is so slow that they may easily be perturbed by passing stars and the galactic tide.

title: List of near-parabolic comets
text: The following is a list of comets with a very high eccentricity (generally 0.99 or higher) and a period of over 1,000 years that don't quite have a high enough velocity to escape the Solar System.

title: List of near-parabolic comets

title: Litema
text: Litema (pronounced: /ditʼɪːma/; also spelled "Ditema"; Singular: Tema, Sesotho for "field") is a form of Sotho mural art composed of decorative geometric patterns, commonly associated with the South Sotho tradition today practised in Lesotho and neighbouring areas of South Africa.

title: Litema
text: Basotho women generate litema on the outer walls of homesteads by means of engraving, painting, relief mouldings and mosaic.

title: Litema
text: Typically the geometric patterns are scratched with a forefinger or hair comb into the wet top layer of fresh clay and dung plaster, and are then painted with natural dyes or, in contemporary times, manufactured paint.

title: Litema
text: Patterns resemble objects from the natural world and most often mimic ploughed fields or depict plant and animal life, sometimes associated with clan totems.

title: Litema
text: Litema are not a permanent facade design, but decay in the sun or may be washed away by a heavy rain.

title: Litema
text: It is common for women of an entire village to apply litema on special occasions such as a wedding or a religious ceremony.

title: Minnie Lichtenstein Marcus

title: Minnie Lichtenstein Marcus

title: Minnie Lichtenstein Marcus

title: Minnie Lichtenstein Marcus
text: The Neiman and Marcus families relinquished sales territories in the nascent soft drink concern for $25,000 which they used to found Neiman Marcus, which initially specialized in ready-to-wear women's finery, in Dallas in 1907.

text: The single spent four weeks at number-one on the US "Billboard" Hot 100, making it the longest running number-one single of 1989.

title: Monir Shahroudy Farmanfarmaian

title: Mount Lu
text: Mount Lu or Lushan (, Gan: Lu-san), also known as Kuanglu (匡庐) in ancient times, is situated in the northern part of Jiangxi province in Central China, and is one of the most renowned mountains in the country.

title: Mount Lu
text: It is located primarily in Lushan county-level city in Jiujiang Prefecture, although the northern portions are found in Lianxi District which was formerly known as Lushan District and until 2016 covered the majority of the Mount Lu.

title: Mount Lu
text: The oval-shaped mountains are about 25 km long and 10 km wide, and neighbors Jiujiang city and the Yangtze River to the north, Nanchang city to the south, and Poyang Lake to the east.

title: Mount Lu
text: Its highest point is Dahanyang Peak (大汉阳峰), reaching 1,474 m above sea level, and is one of the hundreds of steep peaks that towers above a sea of clouds that encompass the mountains for almost 200 days out of the year.

title: Mount Lu
text: Mount Lu is known for its grandeur, steepness, and beauty, and is part of Lushan National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1996, and a prominent tourist attraction, especially during the summer months when the weather is cooler.

title: National Peace Jubilee

title: Nice model
text: The Nice ( ) model is a scenario for the dynamical evolution of the Solar System.

title: Nice model
text: It is named for the location of the Observatoire de la Côte d'Azur, where it was initially developed, in Nice, France.

title: Nice model
text: It proposes the migration of the giant planets from an initial compact configuration into their present positions, long after the dissipation of the initial protoplanetary gas disk.

title: Nice model
text: In this way, it differs from earlier models of the Solar System's formation.

title: Nice model
text: This planetary migration is used in dynamical simulations of the Solar System to explain historical events including the Late Heavy Bombardment of the inner Solar System, the formation of the Oort cloud, and the existence of populations of small Solar System bodies including the Kuiper belt, the Neptune and Jupiter trojans, and the numerous resonant trans-Neptunian objects dominated by Neptune.

title: Nice model
text: Its success at reproducing many of the observed features of the Solar System means that it is widely accepted as the current most realistic model of the Solar System's early evolution, although it is not universally favoured among planetary scientists.

title: Nice model
text: Later research revealed a number of differences between the original Nice model's predictions and observations of the current Solar System, for example the orbits of the terrestrial planets and the asteroids, leading to its modification.

text: Additionally, when Google made a Google Doodle for April 15, 2011, in celebration of Charlie Chaplin's 122nd birthday, they collaborated with the Niles Silent Film Museum to produce the short.

title: North Irvington Gardens Historic District
text: The North Irvington Gardens Historic District is a neighborhood and national historic district in Indianapolis, Indiana.

title: North Irvington Gardens Historic District
text: It was placed on the National Register of Historic Places on June 27, 2008.

title: North Irvington Gardens Historic District
text: It is immediately to the north of the Irvington Historic District, which has been on the National Register since 1987, sharing the same east and west boundaries of the older district (Arlington Avenue and Emerson Avenue, respectively), and extending north to 10th and 11th streets.

title: North Irvington Gardens Historic District
text: It is a neighborhood of mostly residential buildings dating primarily from 1910 to 1950, with no one distinctive architectural style, including a house associated with the historic Osborn Farm.

title: North Irvington Gardens Historic District
text: Except for one church, the only buildings contributing to the historic nature of the district are 843 houses and 551 garages.

title: North Irvington Gardens Historic District

title: Northland Mall
text: Northland Mall was a shopping mall located on the north side of Columbus, Ohio, at the intersection of Morse Road and Karl Road.

title: Northland Mall

title: Northland Mall

title: Ohio State Route 51

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: Old Angel Midnight is a long narrative poem by American novelist and poet Jack Kerouac.

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: It was culled from five notebooks spanning from 1956 to 1959, while Kerouac was fully absorbed by his studies of Buddhism and Buddhist philosophy.

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: Kerouac's one dogma was to compose Lucien Midnight strictly in pencil by candlelight.

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: Lucien Midnight differs from his sketching method of writing because it is based upon an aural experience, and not visual.

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: The bookmovie approach was abandoned in 1953 in favor of a different approach he had stylistically achieved by 1956.

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: Kerouac initially experimented with Old Angel Midnight (then called "Lucien Midnight") in 1953 in his diary titled "1953.

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: Notes again."

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: In entries dated from November 20 to December 3, 1953, he made notes on "Lucien Midnight" which was to be originally conceptualized in what he called "book movie" form, when he closed his eyes and projected onto paper a cinematic sense of what he heard.

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: A bookmovie, he explained in Some of the Dharma, is a "prose concentration camera-eye visions of a definite movie of the mind with fade-ins, pans, close-ups, and fade-outs."

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: Kerouac's notes on Lucien Midnight were written while staying in the Lower East Side where he initially heard sounds coming through a tenement window from the wash court below.

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: He then heard voices coming from kitchens of the other occupants in nearby apartment buildings and a man named Paddy arriving home drunk, and even a junky stirring in his bed.

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: Kerouac conceptualized an idea of developing a work based on James Joyce’s experimental novel "Finnegans Wake" (not "Ulysses" as indicated by Ann Charters in her introduction to "Old Angel Midnight" for Grey Fox Press) where the “sounds of the universe” became the chief “plot” with all of its associated “neologisms, mental associations, puns and wordmixes” that stewed a plethora of languages and “nonlanguages.”

title: Old Angel Midnight
text: Kerouac determinedly “scribbled out in a strictly intuitional discipline at breakneck speed” the fledgling prose that would finally comprise the finished book for City Lights's Pocket Poet series eight years later.

title: Operation Bertram
text: Operation Bertram was a major Second World War deception operation practised by the allied forces in Egypt led by Bernard Montgomery in the months leading up to the Second Battle of El Alamein in 1942.

title: Operation Bertram
text: Bertram was devised by Dudley Clarke to deceive Erwin Rommel about the timing and location of the allied attack.

title: Operation Bertram
text: The operation consisted of physical deceptions using dummies and camouflage, designed and made by the British Middle East Command Camouflage Directorate led by Geoffrey Barkas.

title: Operation Bertram
text: These were accompanied by electromagnetic deceptions codenamed "Operation Canwell" using false radio traffic.

title: Operation Bertram
text: All of these were planned to make the enemy believe that the attack would take place to the south, far from the coast road and railway, and about two days later than the real attack.

title: Operation Halyard
text: Operation Halyard (or Halyard Mission), known in Serbian as Operation Air Bridge (Serbian: Операција Ваздушни мост ), was an Allied airlift operation behind enemy lines during World War II.

title: Operation Halyard
text: In July 1944, the Office of Strategic Services (OSS) drew up plans to send a team to Chetniks led by General Draža Mihailović in the German-occupied Territory of the Military Commander in Serbia for the purpose of evacuating Allied airmen shot down over that area.

title: Operation Halyard
text: This team, known as the Halyard team, was commanded by Lieutenant George Musulin, along with Master Sergeant Michael Rajacich, and Specialist Arthur Jibilian, the radio operator.

title: Operation Halyard
text: The team was detailed to the United States Fifteenth Air Force and designated as the 1st Air Crew Rescue Unit.

title: Operation Halyard
text: It was the largest rescue operation of American Airmen in history.

title: Operation Halyard
text: According to historian Professor Jozo Tomasevich, a report submitted to the OSS showed that 417 Allied airmen who had been downed over occupied Yugoslavia were rescued by Mihailović's Chetniks, and airlifted out by the Fifteenth Air Force.

title: Operation Halyard
text: According to Lt. Cmdr. Richard M. Kelly (OSS) grand total of 432 U.S. and 80 Allied personnel were airlifted during the Halyard Mission.

title: Ostrogothic Kingdom
text: The Ostrogothic Kingdom, officially the Kingdom of Italy (Latin: "Regnum Italiae"), was established by the Ostrogoths in Italy and neighbouring areas from 493 to 553.

title: Ostrogothic Papacy
text: The Ostrogothic Papacy was a period from 493 to 537 where the papacy was strongly influenced by the Ostrogothic Kingdom, if the pope was not outright appointed by the Ostrogothic King.

title: Ostrogothic Papacy
text: The selection and administration of popes during this period was strongly influenced by Theodoric the Great and his successors Athalaric and Theodahad.

title: Ostrogothic Papacy
text: This period terminated with Justinian I's (re)conquest of Rome during the Gothic War (535–554), inaugurating the Byzantine Papacy (537-752).

title: Ostrogothic Ravenna
text: Ostrogothic Ravenna refers to the time period in which Ravenna was the capital of the Ostrogothic Kingdom in Italy.

title: Ostrogothic Ravenna
text: Ravenna is a city in Northeastern Italy that served as the capital of the Ostrogothic Kingdom which existed between 493 and 553 CE.

title: Ostrogothic Ravenna
text: During that time Ravenna saw a great renovation, in particular under Theodoric the Great (454–526).

title: Ostrogothic Ravenna
text: During his rule Ravenna saw many of its finest monuments constructed or renovated including the Basilica of Sant'Apollinare Nuovo, the Palace of Theoderic and Mausoleum of Theodoric.

title: Ostrogothic Ravenna
text: Many of these monuments reflected Theodoric's, as well as the Goths as a people, religion of Arian Christianity.

title: Ostrogothic Ravenna
text: Though an Arian Christian himself, Theodoric's rule was a time of religious tolerance in the city of Ravenna.

title: Ostrogothic Ravenna
text: His religious tolerance extended also to forging a balance between the Romans and Goths in Ravenna.

title: Ostrogothic Ravenna
text: Theodoric attempted to model Ravenna as a capital equivalent to that of Rome or Constantinople and as such was a defender of classical antiquity in a western world that saw much of its classical heritage disappearing.

title: Pap (food)
text: Pap , also known as mieliepap (Afrikaans for maize porridge) in South Africa or Sadza in Shona or Isitshwala in Isindebele language in Zimbabwe, or Ogi/ Akamu in Nigeria or phaletšhe in Botswana is a traditional porridge/polenta made from mielie-meal (ground maize) and a staple food of the Bantu peoples of Southern Africa (the Afrikaans word "pap" is taken from Dutch and simply means "porridge").

title: Pap (food)
text: Many traditional Southern Africa dishes include pap, such as smooth maize meal porridge (also called "slap pap" or soft porridge), pap with a very thick consistency that can be held in the hand ("stywe pap" or firm porridge) and a more dry crumbly phuthu pap.

title: Pap (food)
text: Phuthu dishes are usually found in the coastal areas of South Africa.

title: Pearce v. Ham
text: Pearce v. Ham, 113 U.S. 585 (1885) , was an appeal from the Circuit Court of the United States for the Southern District of Illinois regarding a bill filed by Charles I. Ham, the appellee, against Isaac N. Pearce and Andrew J. Kuykendall, the appellants.

title: Pearce v. Ham
text: Originally, one Joseph K. Frick contracted with the County Court of Johnson County in the State of Illinois, where he agreed to build, according to certain plans and specifications, a courthouse for said county at Vienna, the county seat, furnishing the material and completing it by the first Monday of September 1870, in consideration whereof the county court agreed to pay him $38,357 in the bonds of Johnson county, bearing ten percent interest, and due in six years.

title: Pearce v. Ham
text: Frick never did any work on the building, and, owing to some misunderstanding with the county court, abandoned the contract and told Kuykendall that he might go on and build the courthouse if he chose to do so.

title: Pearce v. Ham
text: On September 9, 1869, Kuykendall, as the agent and attorney in fact of Frick, assigned the contract of the latter to Ham and Pearce, Ham being the appellee, and Pearce one of the appellants, who had formed a partnership for the purpose of building the courthouse under said contract.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s0
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: The Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences (PGSS) is one of the Pennsylvania Governor's Schools of Excellence, a group of five-week summer programs for gifted high school students in the state of Pennsylvania.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s1
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: Carnegie Mellon University in Pittsburgh has hosted the program since its inception in 1982.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s10
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: There is at least one event per day and is advertised on the social calendar in the dorm lobby.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s11
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: For many students, the social development gained from the program rivals the scientific knowledge they acquire.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s12
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: The students leave the program with a strong bond; most attend an organized reunion the following year after the 4th week of the program.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s2
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: Most recently, it has been directed by Physics Professor Dr. Barry Luokkala.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s3
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: Participants are required to be Pennsylvania high school students between their junior and senior years and are required to live in the dormitories for the full five weeks of the program.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s4
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: Admission is very competitive - approximately 500 of the most scientifically gifted students in the state compete for 56 to 60 slots in the program.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s5
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: The aim of PGSS is to promote interest in science rather than to advance students' knowledge in a specific area.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s6
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: The curriculum includes five "core" courses in Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Mathematics and Physics, and numerous electives.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s7
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: In addition to taking classes, students are required to participate in a lab course and a research-style team project.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s8
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: The emphasis is on cooperation, rather than competition - students are encouraged to both collaborate with other students on academic work and to interact socially.

doc_id: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences::s9
title: Pennsylvania Governor's School for the Sciences
text: The Residence Life staff provides a number of structured social events to foster friendship and teamwork.

title: Pet Shop Boys discography

title: Picture to Burn

title: Picture to Burn

title: Pingat Jasa Malaysia
text: The Pingat Jasa Malaysia (PJM) (English: Malaysian Service Medal ) is a medal given by the King and Government of Malaysia.

text: Established 3 March 2004, the medal recognizes service by members of the Malaysian Armed Forces during the Malayan Emergency, Second Malayan Emergency, and the Indonesia–Malaysia confrontation.

title: Pingat Jasa Malaysia
text: The medal was also offered for award to members of the Commonwealth forces from Australia, Fiji, India, Nepal, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom who served in Malaysia during the Malayan Emergency and the Indonesia–Malaysia confrontation.

title: Pingat Jasa Malaysia

title: Pingat Jasa Malaysia

title: Pioneer 4
text: Pioneer 4 was an American spin-stabilized unmanned spacecraft launched as part of the Pioneer program on a lunar flyby trajectory and into a heliocentric orbit making it the first probe of the United States to escape from the Earth's gravity.

title: Pioneer 4
text: It carried a payload similar to "Pioneer 3": a lunar radiation environment experiment using a Geiger–Müller tube detector and a lunar photography experiment.

title: Pioneer 4
text: It passed within 58,983 km of the Moon's surface.

title: Pioneer 4
text: However, "Pioneer 4" did not come close enough to trigger its photoelectric sensor.

title: Pioneer 4
text: The spacecraft was still in solar orbit as of 1969.

title: Pioneer 4
text: It was the only successful lunar probe launched by the U.S. in 12 attempts between 1958–63; only in 1964 would Ranger 7 surpass its success by accomplishing all of its mission objectives.

text: "Prayer" peaked at number-three on two United States airplay charts, "Billboard"'s Mainstream Rock Tracks and Modern Rock Tracks charts, as well as peaking at number-fifty-eight on "Billboard"'s Hot 100 and number-fourteen on the Canadian Singles Chart.

title: Preference Pane
text: A Preference Pane (often abbreviated as prefpane) is a special dynamically loaded plugin in Mac OS X.

title: Preference Pane
text: Introduced in Mac OS X v10.0, the purpose of a Preference Pane is to allow the user to set preferences for a specific application or the system by means of a graphical user interface.

title: Preference Pane
text: Preference Panes are the OS X replacement to control panels. Prior to Mac OS X v10.4, collections of Preference Panes featured a "Show All" button to show all the panes in the collection and a customizable toolbar to which frequently-used preference panes could be dragged.

title: Preference Pane
text: In Mac OS X v10.3, the currently-active pane would also be highlighted in the toolbar when it was selected.

title: Preference Pane
text: With Mac OS X v10.4, this functionality was dropped in favor of a plain Show All button and back/forward history arrows.

title: Profile of a Serial Killer
text: The film was released on DVD on 19 October 2004.

title: Proud Prophet
text: Proud Prophet was a simulated war game played by the United States in 1983.

title: Proud Prophet
text: With an ongoing arms buildup against the Soviet Union, President Ronald Reagan and his Administration had a great deal of concern for the U.S. nuclear war plan and what may occur if we did not take action.

title: Proud Prophet
text: If a risk of a war did occur, many Military advisors saw the use of nuclear missiles as the deterring factor when dealing with the Soviet Union.

title: Proud Prophet
text: The idea behind this concept was that Soviet forces would seek ceasefire if the West moved to use nuclear weapons.

title: Proud Prophet
text: The final outcome of the Proud Prophet war game would show the need to resolve global issues in times of war or potential war.

title: Proud Prophet
text: The outcome of an all-out nuclear war is the total destruction of both sides involved, and a death toll nearly reaching half a billion with the remaining dying from starvation or lethal doses of radiation.

title: Proud Prophet
text: The government file for Proud Prophet was not declassified until December 20th, 2012, and was only declassified in part.

title: Proud Prophet
text: While there is no known reason why it was unclassified under the Obama administration.

title: Proud Prophet
text: After being briefed on the strike plan in place, President Reagan was unsatisfied and took measures to simulate a response to the onset of a nuclear war.

title: Proud Prophet
text: The simulation consisted of 200 Military Personnel and Politicians with only twelve days of actual play.

title: Proud Prophet
text: Stretching the twelve days of gameplay over several week periods, Personnel involved in the simulation were forced to make critical strategic and diplomatic decisions to test the effectiveness of the United States strike plan.

title: Proud Prophet
text: Due to heightened tensions with the ongoing Cold War made this simulation the most realistic in United States Military history.

title: Proud Prophet
text: For the first time ever, the Secretary of Defense and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff took part in the game, although their participation was concealed.

title: Proud Prophet
text: One of the main purposes of the simulation was to test the response of the National Command Authority's (NCA) decision making when dealing with many different situations at once.

title: Proud Prophet
text: Although Proud Prophet was intended to help senior officials test their nuclear strategies, it was apparent that many of the concepts in place were incompatible with current Military capabilities.

title: Proud Prophet
text: Many important parts of this simulation saw limited use of de-escalation tactics.

title: Psych
text: Psych is an American detective comedy-drama television series created by Steve Franks and broadcast on USA Network with syndicated reruns on ION Television.

title: Psych
text: It is produced by Franks and Tagline Television's Chris Henze and Kelly Kulchak.

title: Psych
text: The series stars James Roday as Shawn Spencer, a young crime consultant for the Santa Barbara Police Department whose "heightened observational skills" and impressive detective instincts allow him to convince people that he solves cases with psychic abilities.

title: Psych
text: The program also stars Dulé Hill as Shawn's best friend and reluctant partner Burton "Gus" Guster, as well as Corbin Bernsen as Shawn's father, Henry, a former officer of the Santa Barbara Police Department.

title: Pulitzer Fountain
text: Pulitzer Fountain is an outdoor fountain located in Manhattan's Grand Army Plaza in New York.

title: Pulitzer Fountain
text: The fountain is named after newspaper publisher Joseph Pulitzer who died in 1911 having bequeathed $50,000 for the creation of the fountain.

title: Pulitzer Fountain
text: Pulitzer intended his fountain to be "like those in the Place de la Concorde, Paris, France."

title: Pulitzer Fountain
text: The fountain was designed by the architect Thomas Hastings, and crowned by a statue conceived by the sculptor Karl Bitter.

title: Pulitzer Fountain
text: The fountain was dedicated in May 1916.

title: Pulitzer Prize for Music
text: The Pulitzer Prize for Music is one of the seven American Pulitzer Prizes that are annually awarded for Letters, Drama, and Music.

title: Pulitzer Prize for Music
text: It was first awarded in 1943.

title: Pulitzer Prize for Music
text: Joseph Pulitzer did not call for such a prize in his will, but had arranged for a music scholarship to be awarded each year.

title: Pulitzer Prize for Music
text: This was eventually converted into a full-fledged prize: "For a distinguished musical composition of significant dimension by an American that has had its first performance in the United States during the year."

title: Pulitzer Prize for Music
text: Because of the requirement that the composition had its world premiere during the year of its award, the winning work had rarely been recorded and sometimes had received only one performance.

title: Pulitzer Prize for Music
text: In 2004 the terms were modified to read: "For a distinguished musical composition by an American that has had its first performance or recording in the United States during the year."

title: Pulitzer, Inc.
text: Pulitzer Inc. owned newspapers, television stations and radio stations across the United States.

title: Pulitzer, Inc.
text: Founded by Joseph Pulitzer (who also funded the Pulitzer Prizes, which are not affiliated with the company), its papers included the "St. Louis Post-Dispatch," the "Arizona Daily Star" (Tucson), and Chicago's "Daily Southtown" and Lerner Newspapers chain.

title: Purandara Dasa
text: Purandara Dāsa (Kannada: ಪುರಂದರ ದಾಸ ) (1484–1564) was a Haridasa (a devotee - servant of Lord Hari (Vishnu)), great devotee of Lord Krishna (an incarnation of Lord Vishnu) and a saint.

title: Purandara Dasa
text: He was a disciple of the celebrated Madhwa philosopher-saint Sri Vyasatirtha, and a contemporary of yet another great Haridasa, Kanakadasa.

title: Purandara Dasa
text: His Guru, Sri Vyasatirtha himself glorified Purandara Dasa in a song thus: "Dāsarendare purandara dāsarayya" (ದಾಸರೆಂದರೆ ಪುರಂದರ ದಾಸರಯ್ಯ).

title: Purandara Dasa
text: Purandara Dasa was a composer, singer and one of the chief founding-proponents of the South Indian classical music (Carnatic Music).

title: Purandara Dasa
text: In honor of his significant and legendary contributions to Carnatic Music, he is widely referred to as the "Pitamaha" ("lit", "father" or the "grandfather") of Carnatic Music.

title: Purandara Dasa
text: He is respected as an "avatara" (incarnation) of the great sage Narada (a celestial being who is also a singer).

title: Pátria
text: "Pátria" ("Fatherland") is the national anthem of East Timor.

title: Pátria
text: It was first used when East Timor unilaterally declared its independence from Portugal in 1975, moments before the Indonesian invasion.

title: Pátria
text: It was officially adopted as the national anthem when independence of East Timor was restored in 2002.

title: Pátria
text: It is the only national anthem in Southeast Asia not sung in indigenous Southeast Asian language but in Portuguese, a European language and also the co-official language of the country.

title: Qionghai
text: Qionghai () is one of the seven county-level cities of Hainan province, China.

title: Qionghai
text: Although called a "city", Qionghai refers to a large land area in Hainan - an area which was once a county.

title: Qionghai

title: Qionghai

title: Qionghai

title: Qizu Pagoda

title: Quah Chow Cheung

title: Quechuan languages
text: Quechua , also known as runa simi ("people's language"), is an indigenous language family, with variations spoken by the Quechua peoples, primarily living in the Andes and highlands of South America.

title: Quechuan languages
text: Derived from a common ancestral language, it is the most widely spoken language family of indigenous peoples of the Americas, with a total of probably some 8–10 million speakers.

title: Quechuan languages
text: Approximately 13% of Peruvians speak Quechua.

title: Quechuan languages
text: It is perhaps most widely known for being the main language of the Inca Empire, and was disseminated by the colonizers throughout their reign.

title: Querétaro F.C.

title: QuickDraw
text: QuickDraw is the 2D graphics library and associated Application Programming Interface (API) which is a core part of the classic Mac OS operating system.

title: QuickDraw

title: QuickDraw

title: QuickDraw

title: QuickDraw

title: QuickDraw

title: QuickDraw

title: Quince Orchard High School
text: Quince Orchard High School (QOHS), also known as Q.O. High School, is a secondary school located on Quince Orchard Road in an unincorporated area of Gaithersburg in Montgomery County, Maryland, United States.

title: Raglan Castle
text: Raglan Castle (Welsh: "Castell Rhaglan" ) is a late medieval castle located just north of the village of Raglan in the county of Monmouthshire in south east Wales.

title: Raglan Castle
text: The modern castle dates from between the 15th and early 17th-centuries, when the successive ruling families of the Herberts and the Somersets created a luxurious, fortified castle, complete with a large hexagonal keep, known as the Great Tower or the Yellow Tower of Gwent.

title: Raglan Castle
text: Surrounded by parkland, water gardens and terraces, the castle was considered by contemporaries to be the equal of any other in England or Wales.

title: Raglan Castle
text: During the English Civil War the castle was held on behalf of Charles I and was taken by Parliamentary forces in 1646.

title: Raglan Castle
text: In the aftermath, the castle was slighted, or deliberately put beyond military use; after the restoration of Charles II, the Somersets declined to restore the castle.

title: Raglan Castle
text: Raglan Castle became first a source of local building materials, then a romantic ruin, and is now a modern tourist attraction.

title: Raiffeisen Bank International

title: Raleigh Springs Mall

title: Raleigh Springs Mall

title: Ralph W. 'Bud' Leavitt Jr.
text: Ralph W. 'Bud' Leavitt Jr. (1917–1994) was a Maine newspaperman who was executive sports editor of "The Bangor Daily News", and a longtime outdoor columnist recognized statewide.

title: Ralph W. 'Bud' Leavitt Jr.
text: In addition to his writing, Leavitt hosted one of Maine's earliest television shows, which was devoted to fishing, hunting and the out-of-doors.

title: Ralph W. 'Bud' Leavitt Jr.
text: Leavitt's stature within the state was such that columnist Roy Blount Jr. wrote of the Maine sportswriter that he "fishes with Ted Williams and Red Smith – or, rather, they trout-fish with him."

title: Ralph W. 'Bud' Leavitt Jr.
text: An early conservationist and son of a paper mill union leader, Leavitt urged the state of Maine to acquire lands for public use; one such preserve is today named for the sportswriter and television personality.

title: Ralph Wiggum
text: Ralph Wiggum is a recurring character on the animated series "The Simpsons", voiced by Nancy Cartwright.

title: Ralph Wiggum
text: The son of Police Chief Wiggum and a classmate of Lisa Simpson, Ralph is best known as the show's resident oddball, and is noted for his non sequiturs and erratic behavior.

title: Ralph Wiggum
text: His lines range from nonsensical, or bizarre interpretations of a current event, to surprisingly profound statements that go over people's heads; and his behavior varies between blissfully unaware, to dim-witted, to awkwardly spontaneous, even occasionally straightforward.

title: Ralph Wiggum
text: The very nature of the character has undergone seemingly differing interpretations over the years and within various media.

title: Ramiro Arrue
text: Ramiro Arrue y Valle, generally known as Ramiro Arrue (born 20 May 1892 in Bilbao, died on 1 April 1971 in Saint-Jean-de-Luz) was a Basque painter, illustrator, and ceramist, of Spanish nationality, who devoted his work to the Basque Country.

title: Rancho Cucamonga, California
text: Rancho Cucamonga is a suburban city situated at the foothills of the San Gabriel Mountains in San Bernardino County, California.

title: Rancho Cucamonga, California
text: It is located 37 mi east of Downtown Los Angeles.

title: Rancho Cucamonga, California
text: The city had a population of 165,269 in 2010 and an estimated population of 174,305 in 2014.

text: The city experiences an average of 287 sunny days per year, compared to a national average of 205 days.

title: Rancho Cucamonga, California
text: Its climate is classified as warm Mediterranean, or "Csa", under the Köppen climate classification system.

title: Rancho Cucamonga, California
text: The city's seal, which centers on a cluster of grapes, alludes to the city's agricultural history and intimate connections to wine-making.

title: Ravenna

title: Ravenna

title: Ravenna
text: It then served as the capital of the Ostrogothic Kingdom until it was re-conquered in 540 by the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire.

title: Ravenna
text: Afterwards, the city formed the centre of the Byzantine Exarchate of Ravenna until the invasion of the Lombards in 751, after which it became the seat of the Kingdom of the Lombards.

title: Reek Sunday
text: Reek Sunday (Irish: "Domhnach na Cruaiche" ) or Garland Sunday is an annual day of pilgrimage in Ireland.

title: Reek Sunday
text: On the last Sunday in July, pilgrims climb Ireland's holiest mountain, Croagh Patrick (764 metres) in County Mayo.

title: Reek Sunday
text: It is held in honour of Saint Patrick who, in the year 441, spent 40 days fasting on the mountain.

title: Reek Sunday
text: Masses are held at the summit, where there is a small chapel.

title: Reek Sunday
text: Some climb the mountain barefoot, as an act of penance, and some carry out 'rounding rituals', which were formerly a key part of the pilgrimage.

title: Reek Sunday
text: This involves praying while walking sunwise around features on the mountain.

title: Reek Sunday
text: They walk seven times around the cairn of Leacht Benáin (Benan's grave), fifteen times around the circular perimeter of the summit, seven times around Leaba Phádraig (Patrick's bed), and then seven times around three ancient cairns known as Reilig Mhuire (Mary's cemetery).

title: Research Triangle

title: Sanheyuan
text: Sanheyuan (Chinese: 三合院; pinyin: "sānhéyuàn"; Wade–Giles: "san-ho-yüan") is a historical type of residence that was commonly found throughout China.

title: Sanheyuan
text: Sanheyuan have structures on three sides of a courtyard, forming an inverted U-shape, resembling the Chinese character 凹 (pinyin: "āo").

title: Sanheyuan
text: There is normally a wall linking the two forward-thrusting side wings, called 廂房 (pinyin: "xiāngfáng"), similar to the wings of a siheyuan.

title: Sanheyuan
text: Sanheyuan may be square or rectangular shaped and can be single or multiple-story structures.

title: Sanheyuan
text: Typically there are three structural divisions within the horizontal building in the U, which is called a "three-jian" building (Chinese: 三間屋; pinyin: "sānjiānwū").

title: Sanheyuan
text: The purpose of this main building varies by region, but typically consists of a central room serving ceremonial needs flanked on either side by a bedroom.

title: Sanheyuan
text: The two wings making up the arms of the U may be long or short, according to need, and provide room for kitchens, toilets, storage, and additional bedrooms.

title: Sanheyuan
text: In Taiwan, the wings of the sanheyuan are called "protecting dragons" (Chinese: 護龍; pinyin: "hùlóng").

title: Sanheyuan
text: Additional "hulong" would typically be added in pairs, placed parallel to the first set and then duplicated as the household grew.

title: Sanheyuan
text: The inner pair of "hulong" were traditionally called "inner protectors" (Chinese: 內護; pinyin: "nèihù"), the second pair "outer protectors" (Chinese: 外護; pinyin: "wàihù"), and so on.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: Sea turtle migration refers to the long-distance movements of sea turtles (superfamily Chelonioidea) notably as adults but may also refer to the offshore migration of hatchings.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: Sea turtle hatchings emerge from underground nests and crawl across the beach towards the sea.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: The ability of adult sea turtles to travel to precise targets has led many to wonder about the navigational mechanisms used.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: Some have suggested that juvenile and adult turtles might use the Earth's magnetic field to determine their position.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: There is evidence for this ability in juvenile green sea turtles.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: They then maintain an offshore heading until they reach the open sea.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: The feeding and nesting sites of adult sea turtles are often distantly separated meaning some must migrate hundreds or even thousands of kilometres.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: Several main patterns of adult migration have been identified.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: Some such as the green sea turtle shuttle between nesting sites and coastal foraging areas.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: The loggerhead sea turtle uses a series of foraging sites.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: Others such as the leatherback sea turtle and olive ridley sea turtle do not show fidelity to any specific coastal foraging site.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: Instead, they forage in the open sea in complex movements apparently not towards any goal.

title: Sea turtle migration
text: Although the foraging movements of leatherbacks seem to be determined to a large part by passive drift with the currents, they are still able to return to specific sites to breed.

text: The stout whiting, "Sillago robusta" (also known as the yellow-cheek whiting and school whiting), is a species of benthic marine fish in the smelt-whiting family Sillaginidae.

title: Stout whiting
text: Like other sillaginids, it is an elongate, slightly compressed fish, growing to a maximum known length of 30 cm.

title: Stout whiting
text: The stout whiting is endemic to Australia, with the species divided into western and eastern populations, with the western population ranging from Shark Bay to Fremantle and the eastern population from Bustard Head, Queensland to northern New South Wales.

title: Stout whiting
text: The species inhabits deep, sandy continental shelf regions to a depth of at least 70 m.

title: Stout whiting
text: The stout whiting is a benthic carnivore, consuming a variety of polychaetes and crustaceans.

title: Stout whiting
text: The species grows rapidly, and sexual maturity is reached at a length of 13 cm, with spawning occurring between December and March.

title: Stout whiting
text: Juveniles of the eastern population move to protected inshore waters, while those of the western population remain offshore their entire life.

title: Stout whiting
text: Stout whiting are the subject of a major export fishery operating out of southern Queensland and to a lesser extent New South Wales, with fishery authorities limiting the yearly catch to 1000 tonnes in Queensland.

title: Stout whiting

text: Super Bowl XXVII was an American football game between the American Football Conference (AFC) champion Buffalo Bills and the National Football Conference (NFC) champion Dallas Cowboys to decide the National Football League (NFL) champion for the 1992 season.

title: Super Bowl XXVII
text: The Cowboys crushed the Bills by the score of 52–17, winning their third Super Bowl in team history, and their first one in fifteen years.

title: Super Bowl XXVII
text: This game is tied with Super Bowl XXXVII as the second highest scoring Super Bowl ever with 69 combined points.

title: Super Bowl XXVII
text: The Bills became the first team to lose three consecutive Super Bowls, and just the second team to play in three straight (the Miami Dolphins played in Super Bowls VI–VIII, winning VII and VIII).

title: Super Bowl XXVII
text: The game was played on January 31, 1993 at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, California, the seventh and most recent Super Bowl (until 2022 when Los Angeles hosts again) that the Greater Los Angeles Area has hosted.

title: Super Bowl XXVIII
text: Super Bowl XXVIII was an American football game between the National Football Conference (NFC) champion Dallas Cowboys and the American Football Conference (AFC) champion Buffalo Bills to decide the National Football League (NFL) champion for the 1993 season.

title: Super Bowl XXVIII
text: The Cowboys defeated the Bills by the score of 30–13, winning their fourth Super Bowl in team history, tying the Pittsburgh Steelers and the San Francisco 49ers for most Super Bowl wins.

title: Super Bowl XXVIII
text: The game was played on January 30, 1994, at the Georgia Dome in Atlanta, Georgia.

title: Super Bowl XXVIII
text: Since the 1993 regular season was conducted over 18 weeks (two byes per team), the traditional bye week between the conference championship games and the Super Bowl was removed.

title: Super Bowl XXVIII
text: This was only the third Super Bowl with only one week after that conference title games; the others were Super Bowl IV and Super Bowl XVII.

title: Super Bowl XXXVII
text: Super Bowl XXXVII was an American football game between the American Football Conference (AFC) champion Oakland Raiders and the National Football Conference (NFC) champion Tampa Bay Buccaneers to decide the National Football League (NFL) champion for the 2002 season.

title: Super Bowl XXXVII
text: The Buccaneers defeated the Raiders by the score of 48–21, tied with Super Bowl XXXV for the seventh largest Super Bowl margin of victory, and winning their first ever Super Bowl.

title: Super Bowl XXXVII
text: The game, played on January 26, 2003 at Qualcomm Stadium in San Diego, California, was the sixth Super Bowl to be held a week after the conference championship games (XVII, XXV, XXVIII, XXXIV, and XXXVI).

title: Super Bowl XXXVII
text: It was also the last Super Bowl played in the month of January.

title: Super Bowl XXXVII
text: Super Bowl XXXVI was the first to be played in February, due to the NFL postponing games for a week after the September 11 attacks.

title: Super Bowl XXXVII
text: Starting with Super Bowl XXXVIII in 2004, the Super Bowl has been permanently played in February.

title: Super Bowl XXXVII
text: This was the last Super Bowl until Super Bowl 50 to take place in California.
