text: Heritage Victoria reports to the Heritage Council who assess nominations to the register.

title: Victorian Heritage Register
text: The Minister for Planning is the responsible Minister for Heritage Victoria and the Heritage Act 1995.

title: Victorian Heritage Register
text: As of 2013, there were over 2,200 places and objects listed on the VHR.

title: Viglen
text: Viglen Ltd provides IT products and services, including storage systems, servers, workstations and data/voice communications equipment and services.

title: Vipra Narayana
text: Vipra Narayana (Telugu:విప్రనారాయణ) is a Telugu devotional & biographical film, based on the life of Thondaradippodi Alvar, also called Vipranarayanar or Bhaktanghri Renu Swamy was a Tamil Vaishnava Saint.

title: Vipra Narayana
text: He led his life in devotion to Lord Narayana and worked for the Perumal (Lord) by dedicating him with garlands.

title: Vipra Narayana
text: He is one of the 12 Alvars.

title: Virginia State Route 51
text: State Route 51 (SR 51) is a primary state highway in the U.S. state of Virginia.

title: Virginia State Route 51
text: Known as Westover Drive, the state highway runs 6.20 mi between a pair of intersections with U.S. Route 58 Business (US 58 Business) in Pittsylvania County west of Danville and within Danville.

title: Virginia State Route 51
text: SR 51 is the original alignment of US 58 through the western part of Danville.

title: Virginia State Route 895
text: State Route 895 (SR 895), also known as the Pocahontas Parkway and Pocahontas 895, is a primary state highway in the U.S. state of Virginia.

title: Virginia State Route 895
text: It connects the junction of Interstate 95 and State Route 150 in Chesterfield County with Interstate 295 near Richmond International Airport in Henrico County, forming part of a southeastern bypass of Richmond.

title: Virginia State Route 895
text: Due to a quirk in the evolution of the road, the long-planned designation of Interstate 895 could not be used.

title: Visions of Gerard
text: Visions of Gerard is a 1963 novel by American Beat writer Jack Kerouac.

title: Visions of Gerard
text: It is the first volume in Kerouac's "Duluoz Legend".

title: Visions of Gerard
text: Unique among Kerouac's novels, "Visions of Gerard" focuses on the scenes and sensations of childhood as evidenced in the tragically short yet happy life of his older brother, Gerard.

title: Visions of Gerard
text: Kerouac paints a picture of the boy as a saint, who loves all creatures and teaches this doctrine to four-year-old Jack.

title: Visions of Gerard
text: Set in Kerouac's hometown of Lowell, Massachusetts, it is a beautiful but unsettling exploration of the meaning and precariousness of existence.

title: Višegrad
text: Višegrad (, ] ) is a town in eastern Bosnia and Herzegovina resting at the confluence of the Drina and the Rzav river, in the synonymous municipality in Republika Srpska entity.

title: Višegrad
text: The town includes the Ottoman-era Mehmed Paša Sokolović Bridge, a UNESCO world heritage site which was popularized by Ivo Andrić in his novel "The Bridge on the Drina".

title: Višegrad
text: A tourist site called "Andrićgrad (Andrić's Town)", dedicated to Andrić, is located near the bridge.

title: Voice (film)
text: Voice ( also known as Whispering Corridors 4: Voice and Voice Letter) is a 2005 South Korean horror film, and the fourth installment of the "Whispering Corridors" film series.

title: Voice (film)
text: This film was the debut film for its three young actresses, as well as director Choi Ik-Hwan, who had served as an assistant director on the first film of the series.

title: Voice type
text: A voice type is a particular human singing voice identified as having certain qualities or characteristics of vocal range, vocal weight, tessitura, vocal timbre, and vocal transition points ("passaggio"), such as breaks and lifts within the voice.

title: Voice type
text: Other considerations are physical characteristics, speech level, scientific testing, and vocal register.

title: Voice type
text: A singer's voice type is identified by a process known as voice classification, by which the human voice is evaluated and thereby designated into a particular voice type.

title: Voice type
text: The discipline of voice classification developed within European classical music and is not generally applicable to other forms of singing.

title: Voice type
text: Voice classification is often used within opera to associate possible roles with potential voices.

title: Voice type
text: Several different voice classification systems are available to identify voice types, including the German "Fach" system and the choral music system among many others; no system is universally applied or accepted.

title: Volcanic bomb
text: A volcanic bomb is a mass of molten rock (tephra) larger than 64 mm (2.5 inches) in diameter, formed when a volcano ejects viscous fragments of lava during an eruption.

title: Volcanic bomb
text: They cool into solid fragments before they reach the ground.

title: Volcanic bomb
text: Because volcanic bombs cool after they leave the volcano, they are extrusive igneous rocks.

title: Volcanic bomb
text: Volcanic bombs can be thrown many kilometres from an erupting vent, and often acquire aerodynamic shapes during their flight.

title: Volcanic bomb
text: Bombs can be extremely large; the 1935 eruption of Mount Asama in Japan expelled bombs measuring 5–6 m in diameter up to 600 m from the vent.

title: Volcanic bomb
text: Volcanic bombs are a significant volcanic hazard, and can cause severe injuries and death to people in an eruption zone.

title: Volcanic bomb
text: One such incident occurred at Galeras volcano in Colombia in 1993; six people near the summit were killed and several seriously injured by lava bombs when the volcano erupted unexpectedly.

title: Volcano bowl
text: Volcano bowls are ceramic drinkware originally associated with mid-20th century American tiki bars and tropical-themed restaurants.

title: Volcano bowl
text: Drinks served in volcano bowls are typically rum-based, mixed with tropical fruit juices and other liquors such as brandy, vodka, and triple sec, and garnished with fruit.

title: Volcano bowl
text: The Flaming Volcano cocktail is especially associated with this drinkware.

title: Volksbanken und Raiffeisenbanken
text: Volksbanken und Raiffeisenbanken is a brand of co-operative banks in Germany. "

title: Volksbanken und Raiffeisenbanken
text: Volksbank" derives from People's Bank institutes (co-operatives originally created by a local population often based in a town) and "Raiffeisenbanken" refers to banks founded on initiatives by Friedrich Wilhelm Raiffeisen (who was pioneering farmer credit unions).

title: Volksbanken und Raiffeisenbanken
text: Many co-operative banks in Germany have either "Volksbank" or "Raiffeisenbank" in their name – the nationwide services and associations in the co-operative branch of the German financing industry used the compound of the plurals of these words (so it translates as "Peoples banks and Raiffeisen banks").

title: Voodoo Highway
text: Voodoo Highway is the second album of the band Badlands.

title: Voodoo Highway
text: After the first Badlands album, drummer Eric Singer left the band to join KISS, and was replaced by drummer Jeff Martin, who had previously sung lead vocals in the bands Surgical Steel and Racer X.

title: Voodoo Highway
text: Badlands bandmates Greg Chaisson and Jeff Martin later played together in the bands Blindside Blues Band and RedSea.

title: Vélo'v
text: Vélo'v is a bicycle sharing system run by the city of Lyon, France, in conjunction with the advertising company JCDecaux.

title: Vélo'v
text: It has been the pioneer smart bicycle sharing system, previous systems being more ad hoc and run similar to a charity.

title: Vélo'v
text: The relationship with JCDecaux allows the city to provide the service on a cost neutral basis for the city, and at very low cost to users, in return for providing exclusive advertising access on bus shelters and the like.

title: Vélo'v
text: The primary aim is to reduce vehicle traffic within the city.

title: Vélo'v
text: The scheme also aims to reduce pollution, create a convivial atmosphere within the city, and encourage the health benefits of increased activity.

title: Vélo'v
text: Its name is a portmanteau of French "vélo" ("bike") and English "love".

title: Vélo'v
text: The first bicycle sharing system to open in France, after the pioneering 1974 scheme in La Rochelle, its thundering success inspired similar systems in major French and European cities, including Paris' Velib' in 2007.

title: Vélo'v
text: With the success of these two high profile smart bicycle sharing systems a new paradigm of government supporting bike sharing as a part of a public transportation network emerged.

title: Vélo'v
text: It is still the bike share scheme with the second highest market penetration (1 bike per 121 residents) in the world, after the Velib'.

title: W. E. B. Du Bois
text: William Edward Burghardt "W. E. B." Du Bois ( ; February 23, 1868 – August 27, 1963) was an American sociologist, historian, civil rights activist, Pan-Africanist, author, writer and editor.

title: W. E. B. Du Bois
text: Born in Great Barrington, Massachusetts, Du Bois grew up in a relatively tolerant and integrated community.

title: W. E. B. Du Bois
text: After completing graduate work at the University of Berlin and Harvard, where he was the first African American to earn a doctorate, he became a professor of history, sociology and economics at Atlanta University.

title: W. E. B. Du Bois
text: Du Bois was one of the co-founders of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in 1909.

title: WCTF
text: WCTF is a radio station licensed to Family Radio and located in Vernon, CT.

title: WCTF
text: The station operates daytime only on 1170 kHz with 1,000 Watts of power using a two-tower directional antenna system.

title: WCTF
text: In 1992 the station had a construction permit for 2.5 kW.

title: WGMP
text: WGMP (1170 AM, "104.9 The Gump") is an alternative rock formatted radio station that serves the Montgomery Metropolitan Area, in Alabama, USA, broadcasting on the AM band at a frequency of 1170 KHz and via a broadcast translator on the FM band at 104.9 MHz.

title: WKNW
text: WKNW is a sports radio station broadcasting at 1400 kHz on the AM dial serving Sault Ste. Marie, Michigan and Sault Ste. Marie, Ontario, Canada.

title: WKNW
text: The station is currently the ESPN Radio affiliate for the Sault Ste. Marie market, and is the market's only dedicated sports radio station.

title: WKNW
text: According to past editions of the "Broadcasting Yearbook", the station went on the air as WKNW in August 1990, after briefly holding the callsigns WBPW and WDHP before launch.

title: WWVA (AM)
text: WWVA (1170 AM, "NewsRadio 1170") is an American radio station that broadcasts on a frequency of 1170 kHz with studios in Wheeling, West Virginia.

title: WWVA (AM)
text: Its towers were located in St. Clairsville, Ohio.

title: WWVA (AM)
text: It is West Virginia's only class A 50,000 watt clear-channel station, sharing the frequency's Class A status with KFAQ (formerly KVOO) in Tulsa, Oklahoma, and KJNP in North Pole, Alaska.

title: WWVA (AM)
text: WWVA can be heard in most of the eastern two-thirds of the United States at night, as well as most of Canada.

title: WWVA (AM)
text: The station is owned by iHeartMedia, Inc. and uses the on-air nickname "The Big One" (borrowed from sister stations WLW and WTAM).

title: Walmart Canada
text: Wal-Mart Canada Corp. is the Canadian division of Walmart which is headquartered in Mississauga, Ontario.

title: Walmart Canada
text: It was founded on March 17, 1994 with the purchase of the Woolco Canada chain from the F. W. Woolworth Company.

title: Walpole, Massachusetts
text: Walpole is a town in Norfolk County, Massachusetts, United States and also encompasses the entirely distinct entity of Walpole (CDP), with its much smaller area of 2.9 square miles and smaller population of 5,198 at the 2010 census.

title: Walpole, Massachusetts
text: Walpole Town, as the Census refers to the actual town, is located about 13 mi south of Downtown Boston and 23.5 mi north of Providence, Rhode Island.

title: Walpole, Massachusetts
text: The population was 24,070 at the 2010 census.

title: Walpole, Massachusetts
text: Walpole was first settled in 1659 and was considered a part of Dedham until officially incorporated in 1724.

title: Walpole, Massachusetts
text: The town was named after Sir Robert Walpole, "de facto" first Prime Minister of Great Britain.

title: WarGames
text: WarGames is a 1983 American Cold War science fiction film written by Lawrence Lasker and Walter F. Parkes and directed by John Badham.

title: WarGames
text: The film stars Matthew Broderick, Dabney Coleman, John Wood, and Ally Sheedy.

title: WarGames
text: The film follows David Lightman (Broderick), a young hacker who unwittingly accesses WOPR (War Operation Plan Response), a United States military supercomputer originally programmed to predict possible outcomes of nuclear war.

title: WarGames
text: Lightman gets WOPR to run a nuclear war simulation, originally believing it to be a computer game.

title: WarGames
text: The computer, now tied into the nuclear weapons control system and unable to tell the difference between simulation and reality, attempts to start World War III.

title: Warwick Mall
text: Warwick Mall is an enclosed shopping mall in Warwick, Rhode Island, on the north side of Interstate 295 near the junction with Interstate 95.

title: Warwick Mall
text: Composed of more than 1000000 sqft of retail space, it features more than 80 stores and a food court.

title: Warwick Mall
text: The mall opened for business in 1970, with Boston-based Filene's and Jordan Marsh alongside Providence-based Peerless and The Outlet, and national chain Woolworth as initial anchors, JCPenney being later added as a sixth anchor.

title: Waste House
text: Waste House is a building on the University of Brighton campus in the centre of Brighton on the south coast of England.

title: Waste House
text: It was built between 2012 and 2014 as a project involving hundreds of students and apprentices and was designed by Duncan Baker-Brown, an architect who also lectures at the university.

title: Waste House
text: The materials consist of a wide range of construction industry and household waste—from toothbrushes and old jeans to VHS cassettes and bicycle inner tubes—and it is the first public building in Europe to be built primarily of such products.

title: Waste House
text: "From a distance [resembling] an ordinary contemporary town house", Waste House is designed to be low-energy and sustainable, and will be in continuous use as a test-bed for the university's design, architecture and engineering students.

title: Waste House
text: The building has won several awards and was shortlisted for the Royal Institute of British Architects' Stephen Lawrence Prize in September 2015.

title: Watsonville High School
text: Watsonville High School is a high school located in Watsonville, California in Santa Cruz County, and is part of the Pajaro Valley Unified School District.

title: Watsonville High School
text: This is an open campus school, thus students are able to leave and come back after lunch.

title: Watsonville High School
text: However, this has been a problem for many years; too many students skip class and end up either not graduating or having to move to other schools because of their cuts.

title: Watsonville High School
text: The school mascot is Willy the Wildcat.

title: Watsonville High School
text: The school colors are black and gold.

title: Watsonville High School
text: Their most recent rival (in sports) is Pajaro Valley High School, which is also located in Watsonville.

title: Watsonville High School
text: Watsonville High's long-time rival is Aptos High School; football games between the two schools is known as the "Black and Blue Bowl."

title: Watsonville High School
text: Watsonville High School is a large school with over 2,000 students and staff, making it the largest school in the Pajaro Valley Unified School district.

title: Waxahachie Global High School
text: Waxahachie Global High School is a high school in Waxahachie, Texas, founded in 2007 on the historic T.C. Wilemon campus.

title: Waxahachie Global High School
text: It is one of only 91 STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) academies in the state of Texas.

title: Waxahachie Global High School
text: It was additionally granted Early College High School status in 2009 through a partnership with Navarro College, allowing students to earn an associate degree along with their high school diploma.

title: Waxahachie Global High School
text: Recently, as of the start of the 2013-2014 school year, Global High made a partnership with UT Tyler for all the STEM-based college courses offered at Global.

title: Waxahachie Global High School
text: As a public charter school, students from Ellis County and surrounding areas can attend regardless of zoning.

title: Waxahachie Global High School
text: Many students commute from surrounding cities such as Waxahachie, Red Oak, Ennis, Maypearl, Midlothian, Palmer, Italy, Cedar Hill, and Desoto.

title: Waxahachie Global High School
text: Waxahachie Global was named a 2014 "Best High School" by U.S. News & World Report.

title: We Are Smug (album)
text: We Are Smug is a collaborative studio album recorded by Australian singer-songwriter Darren Hayes and producer and songwriter Robert Conley under the pseudonym We Are Smug.

title: We Are Smug (album)
text: Originally intended as an anonymous secret side project for Hayes to experiment with new sounds, the album was given away for free for a limited period via digital download as a gift to fans on Hayes' birthday on 8 May 2009 but all free links have since been removed.

title: We Are Smug (album)
text: Hayes has recently said he intends to commercially release the album with a bonus song at some point in the future.

title: We Are Smug (album)
text: The album is an eclectic and experimental vehicle where Hayes adopted various personas and experimented with vocal delivery and genre in a way he had never done as a mainstream artist.

title: We Are Smug (album)
text: It is unique as a recording because Hayes shares vocal duties with Conley, sometimes swapping out the lead for backing vocals.

title: We Are Smug (album)
text: Hayes takes the lead on about half the album at varying times changing his voice, alternating between a high falsetto, a lower raspy tone, experimenting with hip hop and beach boys styled harmonies.

title: We Found Love
text: "We Found Love" is a song recorded by Barbadian singer Rihanna from her sixth studio album, "Talk That Talk" (2011).

title: We Found Love
text: It was written and produced by, and features Scottish DJ Calvin Harris; the song was also featured on his third album "18 Months" (2012).

title: We Found Love
text: "We Found Love" premiered on September 22, 2011, on the Capital FM radio station in the United Kingdom, and was made available to download on the same day as the lead single from "Talk That Talk".

title: We Found Love
text: "We Found Love" is an uptempo electro house song, with elements of techno and Europop.

title: We Found Love
text: The song's lyrics speak of a couple who "found love in a hopeless place".

title: Weeratunge Edward Perera
text: Weeratunge Edward Perera ( ) (22 June 1898 – 23 September 1982) was a Malaysian Sinhalese educator, businessman and social entrepreneur.

title: Weeratunge Edward Perera
text: He brought some semblance of peace to Teluk Anson (now Teluk Intan, Perak, Malaysia) during its occupation by the Imperial Japanese Army in World War II and the Malayan Emergency that followed.

title: Weeratunge Edward Perera
text: W. E. Perera oversaw the restoration of water, electrical supplies, medical services and governance to Telok Anson after its invasion by Japanese forces following the withdrawal of the British forces to Singapore.

title: Weeratunge Edward Perera
text: With the surrender of the Japanese and during the tumultuous Malayan emergency that followed, he was responsible in restarting and extending the Anglo Chinese School (ACS), Telok Anson (now Sekolah Kebangsaan Horley Methodist, Teluk Intan) with the help of the returning British administration and local philanthropists.

title: Weeratunge Edward Perera
text: He was the first non Methodist post war principal of the Anglo Chinese School in Telok Anson and was also responsible in organising the first teachers housing cooperative in Malaya at Telok Anson (now the suburb of Kampong Guru (Teacher's Village), Teluk Intan).

title: Wesley Silcox
text: Wesley Silcox (born May 30, 1985, in Santaquin, Utah) is an American professional bull rider.

title: Wesley Silcox
text: He is of English descent.

title: Wesley Silcox
text: He competes in the Professional Rodeo Cowboys Association (PRCA) and Championship Bull Riding (CBR) tour.

title: Wesley Silcox
text: He has qualified for the PRCA's National Finals Rodeo seven times (2005-2008, 2010–11, 2015) and the CBR world finals seven times (2005–10, 2013).

title: Wesley Silcox
text: He was the PRCA world champion bull rider in 2007 and the PRCA Xtreme Bulls Tour champion in 2010.

title: West Alabama Tigers football
text: The West Alabama Tigers football program is the intercollegiate American football team for the University of West Alabama located in the U.S. state of Alabama.

title: West Alabama Tigers football
text: The team competes in the NCAA Division II and are members of the Gulf South Conference.

title: West Alabama Tigers football
text: West Alabama's first football team was fielded in 1938.

title: West Alabama Tigers football
text: The team plays its home games at the 7,000 seat Tiger Stadium in Livingston, Alabama.

title: West Alabama Tigers football
text: The Tigers are coached by Brett Gilliland.

title: West Bromwich Manor House
text: West Bromwich Manor House, Hall Green Road, West Bromwich, B71 2EA, is an important, Grade I listed, medieval domestic building built by the de Marnham family in the late thirteenth century as the centre of their agricultural estate in West Bromwich.

title: West Bromwich Manor House
text: Only the Great Hall survives of the original complex of living quarters, agricultural barns, sheds and ponds.

title: West Bromwich Manor House
text: Successive occupants modernised and extended the manor house until it was described in 1790 as “a large pile of irregular half-timbered buildings, black and white, and surrounded with numerous out-houses and lofty walls.”

title: West Bromwich Manor House
text: The building was saved from demolition in the 1950s by West Bromwich Corporation which carried out an extensive and sympathetic restoration of this nationally important building.

title: Westland Mall (Columbus)
text: Westland Mall was an 860000 sqft shopping center located on the west side of Columbus, Ohio, at the western intersection of U.S. Route 40 and Interstate 270.

title: What Happens Next? (film)
text: What Happens Next?

title: What Happens Next? (film)
text: is a documentary film about the Canadian singer-songwriter, Dan Mangan.

title: What Happens Next? (film)
text: It explores Mangan's ideas on fate and destiny as he's about to perform in his biggest performance to date, a sold out show at the Vancouver, British Columbia Orpheum.

title: What Happens Next? (film)
text: It premiered on CBC Television on August 25, 2012.

title: What Happens Next? (film)
text: The movie was directed and produced by Brent Hodge and Jon Siddall.

title: What Happens Next? (film)
text: It was nominated for a Leo Award in 2013.

title: When I Was Cool
text: When I Was Cool: My Life at the Jack Kerouac School is Sam Kashner's autobiographical account of his experience as the first student at the Jack Kerouac School of Disembodied Poetics, which was founded by Allen Ginsberg and Anne Waldman in honor of their late friend, Jack Kerouac.

title: When I Was Cool
text: As he describes in his book, Kashner was a disgruntled Long Island teenager in the 1970s who was obsessed with the poetry and prose of the Beat generation of the 1950s.

title: Whitehead Light
text: Whitehead Light is a lighthouse on Whitehead Island, on Muscle Ridge Channel, in the southwestern entrance to Penobscot Bay, Maine.

title: Whitehead Light
text: It is in the town of St.George.

title: Whitehead Light
text: Established in 1807, it is one of Maine's oldest light stations, with its present tower built in 1852 to a design attributed to Alexander Parris.

title: Whitehead Light
text: It was listed on the National Register of Historic Places as Whitehead Light Station on March 14, 1988.

title: Whitehead Light
text: The property is now privately owned by Pine Island Camp, which conducts outings to the facility.

title: Whitehead Light
text: The light itself remains an active aid to navigation, maintained by the United States Coast Guard.

title: Whizzgo
text: WhizzGo is a United Kingdom car rental company that provides rental cars in more than 258 countries worldwide.

title: Whizzgo
text: The company started as a pay-by-the-hour service based in the United Kingdom.

title: Whizzgo
text: Since July 2017 it is restructured and is now providing car rental services by price comparing rates of most of the rent-a-car suppliers worldwide.

title: William Bonfield
text: William Bonfield CBE, FREng, FRS (born 6 March 1937) is a British material scientist, and Emeritus Professor of Medical Materials in the University of Cambridge.

title: Williams Park
text: Williams Park is a park located in St. Petersburg, Florida.

title: Williams Park
text: It is the city's first park and encompasses an entire city block between 4th and 3rd Streets North and between 2nd and 1st Avenues North.

title: Williams Park
text: Founded in 1888 and originally named "City Park," it was changed to Williams Park in honor of the founder of St. Petersburg, John Constantine Williams Sr..

title: Winning America
text: Winning America is a documentary television film about the Canadian band Said the Whale.

title: Winning America
text: It follows the band on their first US tour down through California, and then to South by Southwest.

title: Winning America
text: It premiered on CBC Television on July 23, 2011.

title: Winning America
text: The film was directed by Brent Hodge and Thomas Buchan, and was produced by Brent Hodge, Jon Siddall and Sheila Peacock.

title: Winning America
text: It was nominated for a Leo Award in 2012.

title: Winter (TV series)
text: Winter is an Australian mystery-drama-thriller television series which premiered on the Seven Network on 4 February 2015, and concluded on 11 March 2015.

title: Winter (TV series)
text: The series is a spin off of the 2014 telemovie, "The Killing Field".

title: Winter (TV series)
text: It stars Rebecca Gibney and Peter O'Brien reprising their roles from the telemovie.

title: Winter Winds
text: "Winter Winds" is the second single by the London folk quartet Mumford & Sons, released from their debut album, "Sigh No More".

title: Winter Winds
text: It was released in the UK on 6 December 2009, where it peaked at number 44; in Belgium it reached number 29.

title: Winter Winds
text: Marcus Mumford has said that this is his favorite song to sing live.

title: Winter Winds
text: It was written by Winston Marshall.

title: Wishing Stairs
text: Wishing Stairs ( also known as Whispering Corridors 3: Wishing Stairs) is a 2003 South Korean horror film.

title: Wishing Stairs
text: It is the third installment of the "Whispering Corridors" film series set in girls high schools, but, as with all films in the series, is unrelated to the others; apart from a song being sung in one scene that is a pivotal plot in "Voice".

title: Wishing You Were Here
text: "Wishing You Were Here" is a song written by Peter Cetera for the group Chicago and recorded for their album "Chicago VII" (1974), with lead vocals by Terry Kath (uncredited on the original album package), while Cetera sang the song's bridge.

title: Wishing You Were Here
text: The third single released from that album, it reached #11 on the U.S. "Billboard" Hot 100, #9 on the "Cash Box" Top 100, and hit #1 on the Easy Listening chart.

title: Witbank
text: Witbank is a city situated on the Highveld of Mpumalanga, South Africa, within the eMalahleni Local Municipality.

title: Witbank
text: The name Witbank is Afrikaans for "White Ridge" and is named after a white sandstone outcrop where wagon transport drivers rested.

title: Witbank
text: The city is known for the coal-mining in the surrounding region.

title: Women of Wrestling
text: WOW - Women Of Wrestling, aka WOW!

title: Women of Wrestling
text: , is a women's professional wrestling promotion founded in 2000 by David McLane, previously the founder of Gorgeous Ladies of Wrestling.

title: Women of Wrestling
text: It is based in Los Angeles, California, and is owned by McLane and Los Angeles Lakers owner and president Jeanie Buss.

title: Women of Wrestling
text: The promotion launched a series of syndicated programs in the 2000-01 television seasons in 102 TV markets using a similar format of character driven performers, with names befitting a comic book series, such as Jungle Grrrl, an inmate tag-team complete with orange jump suits named Caged Heat, a Hollywood starlet named Lana Star, and the Persian Princess.

title: World Series of Poker Africa
text: The World Series of Poker Africa (WSOPA) is the second expansion effort of World Series of Poker-branded poker tournaments outside the United States.

title: World Series of Poker Africa
text: Since 1970, participants had to travel to Las Vegas if they wanted to compete in the World Series of Poker (WSOP).

title: World Series of Poker Africa
text: Although the WSOP started holding circuit events in 2005 in other states, the main tournaments, which awarded bracelets to the winners, were exclusively held in Las Vegas.

title: World Series of Poker Africa
text: In 2007, the inaugural World Series of Poker Europe marked the first time that a WSOP bracelet was awarded outside of Las Vegas.

title: World Series of Poker Africa
text: In 2010, the WSOP expanded overseas once again, only this time to Gauteng, South Africa.

title: World Series of Poker Africa
text: While the WSOPE awarded bracelets, the WSOPA was considered a circuit event with the winners receiving Championship Rings instead of bracelets.

title: World Series of Poker Africa
text: The WSOPA did not occur in 2011, but the series of tournaments resumed in 2012.

title: World Series of Poker
text: The World Series of Poker (WSOP) is a series of poker tournaments held annually in Las Vegas and, since 2005, sponsored by Caesars Entertainment Corporation (known as Harrah's Entertainment until 2010).

title: World Series of Poker
text: It dates its origins to 1970, when Benny Binion invited seven of the best-known poker players to the Horseshoe Casino for a single tournament, with a set start and stop time, and a winner determined by a secret ballot of the seven players.

title: Xanthoceras
text: Xanthoceras sorbifolium (yellowhorn, shiny leaf yellowhorn, goldenhorn, Chinese flowering chestnut) is a woody perennial in the soapberry family, Sapindaceae, and the only species in the genus Xanthoceras.

title: Xanthoceras
text: It is native to northern China in the provinces of Gansu, Hebei, Henan, Liaoning, Nei Monggol, Ningxia, Shaanxi, and Shandong.

title: Xanthoceras

title: Xanthosoma
text: Xanthosoma is a genus of flowering plants in the arum family, Araceae.

title: Xanthosoma
text: The genus is native to tropical America but widely cultivated and naturalized in other tropical regions.

title: Xanthosoma
text: Several are grown for their starchy corms, an important food staple of tropical regions, known variously as "malanga", "otoy", "otoe", cocoyam (or new cocoyam), "tannia", "tannier", "yautía", "macabo", "ocumo", "macal", "taioba", "dasheen", "quequisque", "ʻ ape" and (in Papua New Guinea) as Singapore taro ("taro kongkong").

title: Xanthosoma
text: Many other species (including especially "X. roseum") are used as ornamental plants, and in popular horticultural literature are known as ‘ape or elephant ear (from the purported resemblance of the leaf to an elephant's ear), although the latter name is sometimes also applied to members with similar appearance and uses in the closely related genera "Caladium", "Colocasia" (i.e., taro), and "Alocasia".

title: Yeardley Smith
text: Martha Maria Yeardley Smith ( ; born July 3, 1964) is a French-American actress, voice actress, writer, author, comedian, and painter.

title: Yeardley Smith
text: She is best known for her long-running role as Lisa Simpson on the animated television series "The Simpsons".

title: Yellow Cab Pizza
text: Yellow Cab Pizza Company is a Filipino chain that retails fast food, primarily pizza.

title: Yellow Cab Pizza
text: In 2001, Yellow Cab Pizza Company was founded by Eric Puno, Henry Lee, and Albert Tan.

title: Yellow Cab Pizza
text: Max's Group, owner of restaurant chain Max's of Manila, owns the brand.

title: Yellow Cab Pizza
text: The restaurant also operates 145 branches in Qatar, United Arab Emirates, and China.

title: Young adult fiction
text: Young adult fiction or young adult literature (YA) is fiction published for readers in their youth.

title: Young adult fiction
text: The age range for young adult fiction is subjective.

title: Young adult fiction
text: Some sources claim it ranges from ages 12–18, while authors and readers of "young teen novels" often define it as written for those aged 15 to the early 20s.

title: Young adult fiction
text: The terms young adult novel, juvenile novel, teenage fiction, young adult book, etc., refer to the works in this category.

title: Young and Innocent
text: Young and Innocent (American title: "The Girl Was Young") is a 1937 British crime thriller film directed by Alfred Hitchcock and starring Nova Pilbeam and Derrick De Marney.

title: Young and Innocent
text: Based on the 1936 novel "A Shilling for Candles" by Josephine Tey, the film is about a young man on the run from a murder charge who enlists the help of a woman who must put herself at risk for his cause.

title: Young and Innocent
text: It is notable for an elaborately staged crane shot Hitchcock devised towards the end of the film, which identifies the real murderer.

title: Yuanyuan Tan

title: Yuanyuan Tan

title: Yuexiu District
text: Yuexiu District is a district in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China, located west of the Tianhe District and east of the Liwan District.

title: Yuexiu District
text: It is the commercial, political and cultural centre of Guangdong and noted for its high quality education.

title: Yuexiu District
text: The Guangdong provincial government and the Guangzhou city government are both located in the Yuexiu District.

title: Yuexiu District
text: Established in 1960, the district absorbed the former Dongshan District in May 2005 along with several former subdistricts of the Baiyun and Tianhe district

title: Zachariah (Supernatural)
text: Zachariah is a fictional character portrayed by Kurt Fuller on The CW Television Network's drama and horror television series "Supernatural".

title: Zachariah (Supernatural)
text: An angel, he first appears in the fourth season and helps manipulate the series protagonist Sam Winchester into releasing Lucifer onto the Earth.

title: Zachariah (Supernatural)
text: In the fifth season, he attempts to convince Dean Winchester into serving as the human vessel for the archangel Michael to start the apocalypse.

title: Zachariah (Supernatural)
text: The opportunity to play an angel initially excited Fuller because he thought that it would give him the chance to break away from his streak of playing villains.

title: Zachariah (Supernatural)
text: Despite the character turning into an antagonist halfway through his appearances, the actor was very proud of the role.

title: Zachariah (Supernatural)
text: Critical reception for the character has been positive, with his sinister humor being of particular note.

title: Zoi Lygerou
text: Zoi Lygerou is a Greek associate professor of biology at the Medical School University of Patras whose works have been published in such journals as the European Journal of Biochemistry, Journal of Cell Science, the Molecular and Cellular Biology journal, Journal of Biological Chemistry, and both Science and Nature journals among others.

title: Zoi Lygerou
text: In 1991 she got her first degree at the University of Athens followed by a Ph.D. from the University of Heidelberg four years later.

title: Zoi Lygerou
text: She also used to be a postdoc at the Imperial Cancer Research Fund of London under guidance from Paul Nurse.

title: Zoi Lygerou
text: On April 12, 1996 she and her colleagues (along with David Tollervey) have discovered that the minimum amount of enzymes are required for the eukaryotes' ribosomal RNA.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: Zollie Malindi (1924 – 21 April 2008) was a South African trade unionist and anti-apartheid activist.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: His life journey started in the small village of Gqogqora , near Tsomo in the former Transkei.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: After the 1994 elections, Zollie continued working as a member of the ANC, but his declining health forced him to retire alongside his wife, activist Letitia Malindi.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: A day after his death in 2008, Zollie Malindi was awarded the Order of Luthuli by former South African president Thabo Mbeki in recognition of his contribution to the trade union movement.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: While growing up, Zollie became aware of racial segregation.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: Years later, after completing his Teaching Training Diploma, he set off to look for work in Cape Town; but in those days it was not easy for an African male to find employment even with a professional's qualification.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: Zollie became actively involved in the African National Party (ANC) and the South African Communist Party (SACP) in the 1940s.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: As members of the ANC were encouraged to join unions, in no time, Zollie joined the Food and Canning Workers Union (FAWU) where he met political leaders like Oscar Mpetha and Ray Alexander.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: Zollie was a dedicated man and a powerful leader with a commanding presence and a high degree of responsibility.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: At the time of the ANC’s banning in 1960, Malindi was the Western Cape Provincial President.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: Following the passage of the 90-day detention laws in 1963, Malindi was arrested and detained together with Looksmart Ngudle, who was the first person to die in detention.

title: Zollie Malindi
text: In the years after his detention, Zollie became even more involved in the fight against apartheid and subsequently became a mentor to the younger generation of political activists that included well-known political figures such as former Minister of Finance Trevor Manuel.

title: Zumanity
text: Zumanity is a resident cabaret-style show by Cirque du Soleil at the New York-New York Hotel & Casino on the Las Vegas Strip.

title: Zumanity
text: The production was unveiled on September 20, 2003.

title: Zumanity
text: It is the first "adult-themed" Cirque du Soleil show, billed as "the sensual side of Cirque du Soleil" or "another side of Cirque du Soleil".

title: Zumanity
text: Created by René Richard Cyr and Dominic Champagne, "Zumanity" is a departure from the standard Cirque format.

title: Zumanity
text: Intended to be for mature adult audiences only, this show is centered on erotic song, dance, and acrobatics.

title: Zweiohrküken
text: Zweiohrküken (lit.

title: Zweiohrküken
text: "Two-eared chick", English title: Rabbit Without Ears 2) is a 2009 German romantic comedy film, written, produced and directed by Til Schweiger.

title: Zweiohrküken
text: A sequel to 2007's "Keinohrhasen" ("Rabbit Without Ears"), it was co-written by Anika Decker and Schweiger, starring Schweiger and Nora Tschirner as former yellow press reporter Ludo and his girlfriend Anna.

title: Émile Jouguet
text: Jacques Charles Émile Jouguet (5 January 1871, Bessèges (Gard) – 2 April 1943, Montpellier) was a French engineer and scientist, whose name is attached to the Chapman–Jouguet condition.

title: Órlaith
text: Órlaith (older spelling: Órfhlaith, newer spelling: Órla) is an Irish language female given name.

title: Órlaith
text: Orlagh is a hybrid spelling based on a merger with another suffix.

title: Órlaith
text: The meaning of the name dervies from Ór, meaning "Golden" and Flaith, meaning "prince" although as names with "flaith" suffixes are almost always exclusively feminine, this is usually interpreted as meaning "princess".

title: Órlaith
text: The retention of the 'fh' within the spelling maintains the ability to easily derive the true meaning of the name, but as this is silent, it is common to see this redacted.

title: Órlaith
text: All spellings of the name are however pronounced the same, as "OR-la".
